Find the most items that can be made
Fill and read a sales record
traps: Don't use only one ingredient; the one that runs out first decides.
Don't take the larger answer; take the smallest.

topics.t: True or false? Testing number statements
topics.h: 'Doubling a number always makes it even.' Is that always true, sometimes true or never true? Be a maths judge!
p: A number statement can be true (12 ÷ 4 = 3) or false (12 ÷ 4 = 4).
We can complete a statement to make it true: 7 × ☐ = 56 is true when ☐ = 8.
To test a general claim, try many examples. One counterexample (an example that fails) shows the claim is not always true.
'Always true': odd + odd is even. 'Sometimes true': half of an even number is even (true for 8, false for 6). 'Never true': odd × odd is even.

ex.q: Is 'half of an even number is even' always, sometimes or never true?
st: One example works and one fails

topics.rl: Scientists and judges test claims with evidence — maths does the same with examples!

rv.summary: A number statement can be true or false. To test a general claim, try many examples; one counterexample shows it is not always true.
focus: Decide if a fact is true
Complete a statement to make it true
Say if a claim is always, sometimes or never true
Find a counterexample
remember: Half of an even number is sometimes even
traps: Don't decide from only one example.
Don't confuse the adding rule with the multiplying rule.

topics.h: Can 16 coconuts be shared equally among 3 friends? Among 4? Factors tell you instantly!
p: A factor divides a number exactly, with nothing left over. 4 is a factor of 12 because 12 ÷ 4 = 3.
Factors come in pairs: 12 = 1 × 12 = 2 × 6 = 3 × 4. So the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.
1 is a factor of every number, and every number is a factor of itself.
A number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself, is called a prime number. 7 is prime.

ex.q: Find all the factors of 18.
st: 4 and 5 do not divide 18 exactly; after 3 × 6 the pairs repeat

topics.rl: Factors help us share sweets equally or arrange chairs in neat rows.

rv.summary: A factor divides a number exactly with nothing left over, and factors come in pairs. A number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself, is a prime number.
focus: Test whether a number is a factor
List all factors using pairs
Spot prime numbers
remember: 1 is a factor of every number; every number is a factor of itself
traps: Don't forget 1 and the number itself.
Not every odd number is prime: 9 = 3 × 3.
Don't list multiples like 30 as factors of 15.

topics.h: Coconuts are sold in bundles of 6. Can a shop sell exactly 40? Multiples will tell you!
p: Multiples of a number are the answers in its times table: multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, …
Multiples go on forever. The first multiple of a number is the number itself.
If 3 is a factor of 12, then 12 is a multiple of 3.
Skip counting gives multiples: counting in 5s gives 5, 10, 15, 20, …

ex.q: Write the first 5 multiples of 6.

topics.rl: Packets of 6 bananas, boxes of 12 eggs and weeks of 7 days all give multiples.

rv.summary: Multiples of a number are the answers in its times table and go on forever. If 3 is a factor of 12, then 12 is a multiple of 3.

Find the nth multiple
Count multiples in a range
Use the words factor and multiple correctly
remember: The first multiple of a number is the number itself

Don't mix up factor and multiple.

topics.h: Fold a paper butterfly down the middle. Both wings match perfectly! That fold is magic: it is a line of symmetry.
p: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly, like mirror images.
If you fold along the line, one half sits exactly on the other.
Some shapes have many lines: a square has 4, an equilateral triangle has 3, a rectangle that is not a square has 2.
A circle has endless lines of symmetry: every line through its centre works.
Some shapes and letters have no line of symmetry, like the letters F and S.

ex.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
st: Fold it down the middle (up and down): halves match
Fold it across the middle: halves match
Fold along each of the 2 corner-to-corner lines: halves match

topics.rl: Rangolis, the Taj Mahal, leaves and butterflies all show lines of symmetry.

rv.summary: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match like mirror images when folded. A square has 4, an equilateral triangle 3, a rectangle 2 and a circle endless lines.
focus: Count lines of symmetry of common shapes
Find letters with and without lines of symmetry
Explain what a line of symmetry is
remember: Square: 4 lines; equilateral triangle: 3; non-square rectangle: 2
A circle has endless lines: every line through its centre
F and S have no line of symmetry
traps: Don't forget the corner-to-corner lines of a square.
A rectangle does not have the diagonal lines.
A letter that matches after a turn (S) need not have a fold line.

topics.t: Letter cut-outs: one fold or two
topics.h: Fold a paper once, draw half of the letter A, cut, open — a whole A! Can you cut an H with two folds?
p: A letter with a vertical line of symmetry (A, M, T, U, V, W, Y) can be cut by folding once and drawing only half.
A letter with a horizontal line of symmetry (B, C, D, E, K) can be cut with a fold across the middle.
Letters with both lines (H, I, O, X) can be cut with two folds, drawing only a quarter.
Some letters (F, G, J, L, P, R) have no line of symmetry, so folding does not help.
The fold always becomes a line of symmetry of the cut-out.

ex.q: Which letters can be cut with two folds, drawing just a quarter: H, A, E or X?
st: Two folds need both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry
A has only vertical, E only horizontal

topics.rl: Decorations for Diwali and school charts are often made by folding paper and cutting once.

rv.summary: Letters with a vertical line of symmetry can be cut with one vertical fold, letters with a horizontal line with one fold across, and letters with both lines with two folds, drawing a quarter.
focus: Sort letters by vertical, horizontal or both lines
Decide how to fold to cut a letter
Find letters that cannot be made by folding
remember: Vertical line: A, M, T, U, V, W, Y
Horizontal line: B, C, D, E, K
Both: H, I, O, X; none: F, G, J, L, P, R

Two folds mean drawing a quarter, not a half.

topics.h: Can you finish half a rangoli so it looks perfect? Let's make designs like an artist!
p: To complete a design with a mirror line, copy each part to the other side of the line.
Each point and its mirror image are the same distance from the line, on opposite sides.
On grid paper, count squares from the line to place the image exactly.
Fold-and-cut paper designs always have a line of symmetry along the fold.

ex.a: 3 squares to the right of the line, in the same row

topics.rl: Kolam and rangoli artists, tailors and kite makers all build symmetrical designs.

Find the size or count of a completed design

topics.h: Spin a pinwheel. It looks the same again and again before it finishes one full turn! That is turn symmetry.
p: Some designs look exactly the same after a part of a full turn. This is turn (rotational) symmetry.
Count how many times a design looks the same in one full turn.
A square looks the same 4 times in a full turn, after every 90°.
An equilateral triangle looks the same 3 times (every 120°). A rectangle that is not a square looks the same 2 times (every 180°).
Letters like S, N and Z look the same after a half turn (180°).

st: It looks the same 3 times in a full turn

topics.rl: Fans, wheels, flowers, rangolis and chakra designs show turn symmetry.

Count how many times a shape matches in a full turn
Spot letters that match after a half turn

S, N and Z match after a half turn

Don't confuse turn symmetry with a mirror line.

topics.h: Spin a paper firki slowly. At which turns does it look exactly as it started?

A 4-blade windmill looks the same after every 1/4 turn.
Some designs match after a 1/2 turn but NOT after a 1/4 turn — like a rectangle or the letter S.
A shape can have rotational symmetry without any line of symmetry, like a windmill whose blades all bend the same way, or the letters S, N, Z.
Every shape looks the same after a full turn, so we only count smaller turns as rotational symmetry.

ex.a: Only at the 1/2 turn (and the full turn)

topics.rl: Fans, wheels, flowers and windmills all have rotational symmetry.

Find shapes with turn symmetry but no fold line

topics.h: Turn your notebook upside down: 69 is still 69! Which other numbers can do tricks like this?
p: Digits written in a simple way: 0 and 8 have a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry, and look the same after a 1/2 turn.
3 has a horizontal line of symmetry only. 1 written as a straight stick has both lines and a 1/2-turn symmetry.
6 turned by a 1/2 turn becomes 9, so 69 and 96 look the same after a 1/2 turn — but they have no line of symmetry.
Numbers like 11, 88, 808 and 1001 (with stick 1s) have a vertical line, a horizontal line and 1/2-turn symmetry.
To create a number with 1/2-turn symmetry, use 0, 1, 8 in matching places, or pair 6 with 9.

ex.q: Does 808 look the same after a 1/2 turn? Does it have a vertical line of symmetry?

topics.rl: Some digital clock times like 10:01 look the same in a mirror. Car number plates can hide symmetry too!

Check if a number looks the same after a half turn
Make numbers with half-turn symmetry

topics.h: Can you colour a 3 by 3 square with just two colours so it looks the same after every quarter turn?
p: To test a design for rotational symmetry, trace it, turn the tracing about the centre, and check if it fits.

In a 3 × 3 grid, colouring the 4 corners one colour and the 4 edge squares another gives a 1/4-turn match.

If it matches after 1/4 turn, it also matches after 1/2 turn

topics.h: Take squares and equilateral triangles with the same side length. Join them to make star and flower designs!

A square with a triangle on each of its 4 sides makes a star with 4 lines of symmetry and 1/4-turn symmetry.

Sort designs: reflection only, rotation only, or both.

So the whole design matches after a 1/4 turn

topics.h: Nani wants to sew a lace border all around her quilt. How much lace does she need? That length is the perimeter!
p: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary (the edge all around) of a shape.
To find it, add the lengths of all the sides.
Rectangle: perimeter = length + breadth + length + breadth = 2 × (length + breadth).
Square: all 4 sides are equal, so perimeter = 4 × side.
Perimeter is measured in units of length: cm, m or km.

topics.t: Covering surfaces and choosing area units
topics.h: Try to cover your desk with bangles. Now try with notebooks. Which one leaves gaps?
p: Shapes that cover a surface with no gaps and no overlaps tile it. Squares, rectangles and triangles can; circles always leave gaps.

topics.rl: Architects draw room plans from above with a North arrow, so builders know which way windows face.

focus: Find which wall an object is on from a person's view
Place objects on a room map
Know why a map needs a North arrow
remember: Facing north: right = east, behind = south
Map with North at top: west wall on the left
traps: Don't use the 'facing north' rule when the person faces another way.
Behind is the opposite direction, not west.

topics.h: The school bus goes from Ravi's house to the zoo. Turn left, go straight, turn right… can you follow it?
p: Describe a route with directions, turns (left/right) and road names: 'Go north on Gandhi Road, turn right into Nehru Road.'
A right turn is a quarter turn clockwise; a left turn is a quarter turn anticlockwise.
To find places in a direction from a house, look on that side of the house on the map.
Trace a route on a map with your finger or a pencil, stop by stop.
To decide which stop is nearer, count blocks or compare distances.

ex.q: Ravi walks north on Gandhi Road and turns right into Nehru Road. Which direction is he walking now?

topics.rl: Bus drivers, delivery riders and taxi drivers follow routes with turns every day.

rv.summary: Describe a route with directions, left and right turns and road names. A right turn is clockwise and a left turn anticlockwise; trace the route stop by stop and count blocks to compare distances.
focus: Find the new direction after a turn
Reverse a route
Find which stop is nearer
remember: North + right turn → east; east + left turn → north
To return, undo the last move first in the opposite direction
traps: Left does not always mean west.
Don't repeat a route when you need to reverse it.

topics.h: Imagine you are a bird flying over your town. What you see from up there is what a map shows!
p: A map is a drawing of a place as seen from above (a bird's-eye view).
A map is much smaller than the real place.
The key (legend) tells what each symbol on the map means.
Most maps have North at the top.
Grid maps use a letter for the column and a number for the row, like B4, to find places quickly.

ex.q: On a grid map, columns are A to E (left to right) and rows are 1 to 5 (top to bottom). The temple is in column C, row 2. How do we name its square?
st: Write the column letter first: C

topics.rl: Maps help us find a shop in a mall, a platform at a railway station or a route on a phone.

rv.summary: A map is a bird's-eye drawing of a place, much smaller than the real place. The key explains the symbols, most maps have North at the top, and grid maps name squares by column letter then row number.
focus: Use a map key
Name grid squares like B4
Move between grid squares
Choose good landmarks
remember: Column letter first, then row number
Most maps have North at the top
traps: Don't swap column and row.
Don't count the starting square when counting moves.

topics.h: A metro map uses coloured lines. Where two lines meet, you can change trains — that is an interchange!
p: Each metro line has a colour and a list of stations in order.
An interchange station is where two lines meet. You change trains there.
Example map — Red Line: Anand, Bagh, City Centre, Dairy, Eastgate. Blue Line: Fort, Ganga, City Centre, Hill, Ishan.
To go from Anand to Hill: Red Line to City Centre (change), then Blue Line to Hill.
Count the stations to choose the route with the fewest stops.

ex.q: Using the map above, how many stops from Anand to Hill?
st: Change to Blue: City Centre → Hill (3)

topics.rl: The Delhi Metro has many coloured lines like Yellow, Blue and Violet with interchange stations like Rajiv Chowk.

rv.summary: Each metro line has a colour and stations in order. An interchange is where two lines meet and you change trains; count stations to find the route with the fewest stops.
focus: Find the interchange
Count stops on one or two lines
Choose the best route
remember: Anand → Hill: Red to City Centre, change, Blue to Hill: 3 stops
traps: Don't count the starting station as a stop.
Don't count the interchange twice.
Don't change lines when both stations are on one line.

topics.t: Making a school map and a treasure hunt
topics.h: Hide a treasure in your school and draw a map so your friends can find it!
p: A school map shows buildings and places from above: classrooms, playground, office, library.
Make a key: choose a simple symbol for each place (□ classroom, ✚ first aid, 🌳 tree).
Draw a North arrow and keep places in the right positions compared with each other.
For a treasure hunt, mark the hidden object with ✖ and give direction clues: '10 steps east of the tap.'
Check your map by asking a friend to follow it.

ex.q: Your map key says ▲ = water tap. A ✖ is drawn just east of ▲. Where is the treasure?
st: East is to the right on a map with North at the top
ex.a: Just to the east of the water tap

topics.rl: Scouts and guides make maps with keys for camps and treasure hunts.

rv.summary: A school map shows places from above, with a key of simple symbols and a North arrow. For a treasure hunt, mark the spot with ✖ and give clues with a landmark, direction and distance.
focus: Make a map key with clear symbols
Place treasure using direction clues
Write a helpful treasure clue
remember: Every good map needs a key and a North arrow
A good clue: '5 steps east of the water tap'
North at top: north up, west left
traps: Vague clues like 'near something' do not help.
Don't mix up west (left) and east (right).

topics.h: An ant walks 2 cm north and 3 cm east to reach the sugar. Is there more than one way? Which is shortest?
p: On a grid, describe moves with distance and direction: '2 cm north, then 3 cm east'.
There can be many routes to the same point: 3 cm east then 2 cm north also works.
The shortest routes along grid lines never go backwards. For 2 north and 3 east, every shortest route is 5 cm.
A route that goes south and then north again is longer.
To return home, reverse the moves: 3 cm west, then 2 cm south.

ex.q: An ant goes 4 cm east, 1 cm north, 2 cm west and 1 cm north. How far is it from the start, and in which directions?
ex.a: 2 cm east and 2 cm north of the start

topics.rl: Delivery riders look for the shortest route through the lanes of a town, just like the ant!

rv.summary: On a grid, describe moves by distance and direction. Many routes reach the same point; the shortest never go backwards, and you return home by reversing the moves.
focus: Find the length of a grid route
Find the shortest route length
Find position after several moves
Reverse a route
remember: Shortest route = north–south distance + east–west distance
4 E, 1 N, 2 W, 1 N → 2 cm east, 2 cm north
Home from 2 N, 3 E: 3 W, then 2 S
traps: Don't multiply distances; add them.
Going backwards makes a route longer.
East and west cancel; subtract them.

topics.h: The lion is at (3, 2) and the tiger at (2, 3). Are they in the same place? No! The order matters.
p: On a grid, a pair of numbers gives a position: the first number tells how far across, the second how far up.
(3, 2) means 3 across and 2 up. (2, 3) means 2 across and 3 up — a different spot!
To find the animal at a position, start at (0, 0), called the origin, go across, then up.
To write an animal's position, count across first, then up.
To plot a point, start at 0, move across, then up, and mark a dot.

ex.q: Zoo grid: Lion (3, 2), Elephant (1, 4), Zebra (4, 1). Which animal is 1 across and 4 up?

topics.rl: Seats in a cinema (row and number) and squares on a chessboard are found with pairs of letters or numbers too.

rv.summary: On a grid, a pair of numbers gives a position: the first number is how far across and the second how far up, starting from (0, 0). The order matters.
focus: Read and write positions like (3, 2)
Find an animal at a position
Plot points and move them
remember: Moving right changes the first number; moving up changes the second
traps: Don't read up first.
0 across means do not move across at all.

topics.h: How can a whole state fit on one page? The secret is the map scale!
p: A map scale tells how much real distance 1 cm on the map stands for.
If 1 cm = 5 km, then 4 cm on the map is 4 × 5 = 20 km in real life.
Real distance = map length × the scale distance.
Map length = real distance ÷ the scale distance.
Always write the units: cm on the map, m or km in real life.

ex.q: On a map, 1 cm stands for 5 km. Two towns are 4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?

topics.rl: Road atlases, school plans and phone maps all use scales. Zooming in on a phone changes the scale!

rv.summary: A map scale tells how much real distance 1 cm on the map stands for. Real distance = map length × scale distance; map length = real distance ÷ scale distance.
focus: Find real distance from a map
Find map length from real distance
Compare maps with different scales
remember: Map length = real distance ÷ scale distance
Write cm on the map and m or km in real life
traps: Don't add the map length and the scale.
Don't multiply when finding map length; divide.
A bigger number in the scale makes things look smaller.

topics.h: Class 5 did a survey: how do you come to school? Let's be data detectives and find the story in the numbers!
p: Tally marks are drawn in bundles of 5 (four lines and one across) to count quickly.
From data we can find the most, the least, the total and the difference.
We can also find fractions of the data: 20 out of 40 is half.
Only say what the data really shows. Do not guess things it does not tell.

ex.q: 40 children answered: 20 walk, 12 come by bus, 8 cycle. What fraction walk? How many more walk than cycle?
ex.a: Half walk; 12 more walk than cycle

topics.rl: Schools, shops and doctors collect data to make good decisions.

rv.summary: Tally marks are drawn in bundles of 5. From data we can find the most, the least, the total, the difference and fractions, but we only say what the data really shows.
focus: Read tally marks
Find most, least, total and difference
Find a fraction of the data
Pick true statements about data
traps: Don't count a tally bundle as 1.
Don't leave out the smallest number in a total.
'More than 5' does not include 5.

topics.h: Can one little mango picture stand for 5 mangoes? In a pictograph, it can!
p: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols.
The key tells how many things one symbol stands for, like 🥭 = 5 mangoes.
To read it, multiply the number of symbols by the key.
Half a symbol stands for half the key number.
Choose a key that keeps the pictures easy to draw and count.

ex.q: Key: 🍎 = 10 apples. A shop's row shows 🍎🍎🍎🍎 and half an 🍎. How many apples?

topics.rl: Pictographs are used in newspapers, school charts and posters to show data in a fun way.

rv.summary: A pictograph shows data with symbols, and the key tells how many each symbol stands for. Multiply the number of symbols by the key; half a symbol is half the key.
focus: Read a pictograph using the key
Find how many symbols show a number
Choose a good key
traps: Don't count symbols and forget the key.
Don't ignore half symbols or count them as full ones.

topics.t: Two-wheelers on the road: pictographs with a scale
topics.h: Students counted two-wheelers passing their school in 15 minutes. Each 🛵 stands for 3 vehicles!
p: With the scale 🛵 = 3 vehicles, multiply the number of icons by 3.
Pictograph (🛵 = 3 vehicles): Scooters 🛵×6, Motorcycles 🛵×8, Mopeds 🛵×4, E-scooters 🛵×2.
So scooters = 6 × 3 = 18, motorcycles = 24, mopeds = 12, e-scooters = 6. The maximum is motorcycles.
Total = 18 + 24 + 12 + 6 = 60 vehicles. Difference: motorcycles − mopeds = 24 − 12 = 12.
To redraw with 🛵 = 6 vehicles, divide each value by 6: 3, 4, 2 and 1 icons.

ex.q: Using the pictograph, how many more motorcycles than scooters passed?

topics.rl: Traffic police count vehicles at busy crossings to plan signals and lanes.

rv.summary: With a scale like 🛵 = 3 vehicles, multiply icons by 3 to read the data. To redraw with a bigger scale, divide each value by the new scale; the data stays the same.
focus: Read a pictograph with a scale
Find the maximum, total and difference
Redraw with a new scale
traps: Don't subtract icons and forget the scale.
A new scale does not change the real numbers.

topics.h: Asha and Ravi both have 24 hours a day. How differently do they spend them?
p: A table or a picture record can show how much time someone spends on each activity.
Asha: sleep 9 h, school 7 h, play 2 h, study 2 h, TV 1 h, meals 1 h 30 min, other 1 h 30 min. Ravi: sleep 8 h, school 7 h, play 1 h, study 2 h, TV 4 h, meals 1 h, other 1 h.
To compare, find the difference for each activity: Ravi watches TV 4 − 1 = 3 hours more than Asha.
The times in a full day must add up to 24 hours.
A balanced routine has enough sleep, play and study, and not too much screen time.

ex.q: How much more does Asha sleep than Ravi?

topics.rl: Doctors say children your age need about 9–11 hours of sleep and some active play every day.

rv.summary: A table can show how much time someone spends on each activity; a full day adds up to 24 hours. Compare routines by finding the difference for each activity.
focus: Compare time spent on activities
Check that a day adds to 24 hours
Decide which routine is more balanced
remember: Ravi watches TV 4 − 1 = 3 hours more than Asha
Times in a day add up to 24 hours
traps: Don't give one person's time when asked for the difference.
Don't leave out an activity when adding.
More TV does not mean a better routine.

topics.t: A day in my life as a bar graph
topics.h: Turn your whole day into bars! The longest bar shows what you do most.
p: Record your 24-hour routine in hours and minutes. Check that it adds up to 24 hours.
To draw a bar graph: draw two axes, write the activities along one, mark a scale (like 1 square = 1 hour) along the other.
Draw each bar as long as its time. Keep bars the same width with equal gaps.
Strip graph: cut paper strips as long as each measured length (like index fingers) and paste them side by side — it becomes a bar graph.
Give the graph a title and label both axes.

ex.q: Meena's day: sleep 10 h, school 6 h, play 2 h, homework 2 h, meals 2 h, other ? Find 'other'.

topics.rl: Health apps show your sleep and exercise as bars every day.

rv.summary: To draw a bar graph, draw two axes, write the activities on one, mark a scale on the other, and draw equal-width bars as long as each value. A strip graph pastes measured strips side by side.
focus: Find a missing time in a 24-hour day
Find bar length using a scale
Compare lengths in a strip graph
Read a bar using its scale
remember: All bars the same width; add a title and axis labels
traps: Don't ignore the scale.
Compare mm too: 5 cm 5 mm is shorter than 6 cm.
Don't read squares as hours when each is 30 minutes.

topics.h: Which fruit does your class love most? A bar graph shows the winner in one look!
p: A bar graph uses bars of different lengths to show data.
The longer or taller the bar, the bigger the number it shows.
The scale on the side tells what each line stands for, like 1 line = 2 children.
All bars should be the same width with equal gaps between them.
Bars can go up (vertical) or across (horizontal).

ex.q: On a bar graph each line stands for 2 children. The Mango bar reaches 6 lines. How many children chose mango?

topics.rl: Cricket scorecards on TV, rainfall charts and school results often use bar graphs.

rv.summary: A bar graph uses bars of different lengths to show data: the longer the bar, the bigger the number. The scale tells what each line stands for, and bars have the same width and equal gaps.
focus: Find the tallest and shortest bars
Find totals and differences from a bar graph
Read a bar using the scale
traps: Don't read the number of lines without the scale.
Don't leave out a bar when adding.

topics.t: Food wastage in the school canteen
topics.h: Every plate of food left uneaten is food that could have fed someone. A bar graph can show us how much!
p: Food wasted in the canteen (kg): Mon 8, Tue 5, Wed 12, Thu 6, Fri 9.
The tallest bar (Wednesday, 12 kg) shows the most waste; the shortest (Tuesday, 5 kg) shows the least.
Total for the week = 8 + 5 + 12 + 6 + 9 = 40 kg.
Use data in a calculation: if one child eats about 250 g, then 40 kg = 40,000 g could feed 40,000 ÷ 250 = 160 children.
We can predict from data (Wednesday may again be high) and think of ways to reduce waste: take smaller servings, ask for more if hungry, share extra food.

ex.q: Wednesday's waste was 12 kg. If one child eats about 250 g, how many children could that feed?

topics.rl: Many schools now weigh leftover food to help children waste less.

rv.summary: A bar graph of canteen food waste shows the most waste on Wednesday (12 kg) and the least on Tuesday (5 kg), 40 kg in the week. We can calculate, predict and think of ways to reduce waste.
focus: Find most, least, total and difference
Use data in a calculation with kg and g
Make a sensible prediction
Find the average per day
traps: Change kg to g before dividing by grams.
Don't divide by the wrong number of days.

topics.t: True or false? Observing a picture
topics.h: Look carefully at a busy picture and count. Then be a judge: is each statement true or false?
p: Count each kind of item in the picture carefully. Make a quick tally if it helps.
A picture of a park shows: 5 children on swings, 3 dogs, 8 birds, 2 benches, 4 trees and 1 ice-cream cart.
Compare counts to check statements: 'There are more birds than dogs' is true because 8 > 3.
Some statements are opinions ('The park is beautiful') — they cannot be checked by counting.
Only say what the picture really shows.

ex.q: Is 'There are twice as many trees as benches' true?

topics.rl: Detectives and reporters observe carefully and check facts before they write.

rv.summary: Count each kind of item in a picture carefully and compare counts to check statements. Opinions like 'The park is beautiful' cannot be checked by counting.
focus: Check true or false statements by counting
Find how many more
Tell facts from opinions
remember: Birds 8 > dogs 3, so 'more birds than dogs' is true
traps: 'Twice' means 2 times, not 2 more.
Don't mix up 'fewer' and 'more'.
Don't leave out any item when counting all.

qa.q: Count in thousands: 5,000, 6,000, 7,000, … What comes next?
qa.e: Counting in thousands adds 1,000 each time. 7,000 + 1,000 = 8,000.

qa.q: How do we say 4,000 in words?
qa.e: 4,000 has 4 in the thousands place, so it is four thousand.

qa.q: Kavya has nine ₹1,000 notes. Her uncle gives her one more ₹1,000 note. How much does she have now?
qa.e: 9 thousands + 1 thousand = 10 thousands, which is ₹10,000.

qa.q: Which number do these tokens make: 3 ten-thousands, 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 2 tens, 5 ones?
qa.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 for the empty hundreds place: 34,025.

qa.q: Which tokens make 50,608?
qa.e: In 50,608 the 5 is in the ten thousands place, 6 in the hundreds place and 8 in the ones place. The thousands and tens are 0.

qa.q: How many thousands make 10,000?
qa.e: 1,000 + 1,000 + … ten times = 10,000. So 10 thousands make ten thousand.

qa.q: Ravi has 4 ten-thousand tokens and 12 thousand tokens. What number do his tokens show?
qa.e: 4 ten-thousands = 40,000 and 12 thousands = 12,000. Together 40,000 + 12,000 = 52,000.

qa.q: What is 1 more than 9,999?
qa.e: 9,999 + 1 = 10,000, the smallest 5-digit number.

qa.q: How many zeros are there in 1 lakh written as a number?
qa.e: 1 lakh is 1,00,000: a 1 followed by 5 zeros.

qa.q: How many thousands make 1 lakh?
Write 'three lakh six thousand forty' in numbers.
qa.e: 3 lakh = 3,00,000, six thousand = 6,000, forty = 40. Together: 3,06,040. The ten-thousands place is 0.

qa.q: How do we read 4,52,309?
qa.a: Four lakh fifty-two thousand three hundred nine
qa.e: 4 lakh, then 52 thousand, then 309 (three hundred nine).

qa.q: A stadium has 10 stands. Each stand seats 10,000 fans. How many fans can sit in all?
qa.e: 10 groups of 10,000 make 1,00,000, which is 1 lakh.

qa.q: Which number comes just after 99,999?
qa.e: 99,999 + 1 = 1,00,000. It is the first 6-digit number.

qa.q: Arjun has 4 bundles of ₹10,000 and 5 notes of ₹1,000. How much money does he have?
What is the smallest 6-digit number?
qa.e: The smallest 6-digit number is 1 followed by five zeros: 1,00,000.

qa.q: In 5,38,214, which digit is in the ten thousands place?
qa.e: From the right: 4 ones, 1 ten, 2 hundreds, 8 thousands, 3 ten thousands, 5 lakhs.

qa.q: What is the place value of 6 in 2,64,105?
qa.e: 6 is in the ten thousands place, so it is worth 6 × 10,000 = 60,000.

qa.q: What is the place value of 4 in 4,12,380?
qa.e: The 4 is in the lakhs place: 4 × 1,00,000 = 4,00,000.

qa.q: Write 3,00,000 + 50,000 + 700 + 9 as one number.
qa.e: 3 lakhs, 5 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 7 hundreds, 0 tens, 9 ones: 3,50,709.

qa.q: Kabir's fair had 2,07,450 visitors. What does the 0 just after the 2 tell us?
qa.e: The digit after the lakhs digit is in the ten thousands place. 0 there means no ten thousands.

qa.q: What is the place value of 3 in 7,85,312?
qa.e: 3 is in the hundreds place: 3 × 100 = 300.

qa.q: Which number has 9 in the thousands place?
qa.e: In 1,29,450 the places from the right are 0 ones, 5 tens, 4 hundreds, 9 thousands.

qa.q: 5,25,000 has two 5s. What is the difference between their place values?
qa.e: One 5 is in the lakhs place (5,00,000) and the other in the thousands place (5,000). 5,00,000 − 5,000 = 4,95,000.
Each number is 1,111 more than the one before. 3,333 + 1,111 = 4,444.

qa.q: What is the step in this pattern? 5,200, 6,250, 7,300, 8,350
qa.e: 6,250 − 5,200 = 1,050, and every jump is the same.
Each time we subtract 1,001. 12,998 − 1,001 = 11,997.

qa.q: A pattern starts at 40,000 and adds 2,500 each time. What is the third number?
qa.e: 40,000, then 42,500, then 45,000. The third number is 45,000.

qa.q: Which list is in increasing order?
qa.e: Increasing means smallest first. 8,099 < 8,909 < 8,990 < 9,008.

qa.q: On a number line marked 30,000, 31,000, 32,000, between which marks does 31,650 lie?
qa.e: 31,650 is more than 31,000 but less than 32,000.

qa.q: On a number line, which of these numbers is farthest to the left?
qa.e: The smallest number is farthest left. 26,780 is the smallest.

qa.q: Sana counts back in 100s: 10,300, 10,200, 10,100, ___. What does she say next?
Which is greater: 98,765 or 1,02,345?
qa.e: 1,02,345 has 6 digits and 98,765 has only 5, so 1,02,345 is greater.

qa.q: Which symbol goes in the box? 3,45,620 ☐ 3,45,260
qa.e: Lakhs, ten thousands and thousands match. In the hundreds, 6 > 2, so 3,45,620 > 3,45,260.

qa.q: Which is the largest?
qa.e: All have 4 lakhs. In the ten thousands place, only 4,10,000 has a 1, so it is the largest.

qa.q: Harpreet puts 56,000; 5,60,000 and 5,06,000 in order from smallest. Which is in the middle?
qa.e: 56,000 is smallest (5 digits). Then 5,06,000, then 5,60,000.

qa.q: What is the largest 6-digit number made with 3, 0, 7, 1, 9, 5 (each used once)?
qa.e: Put the digits from biggest to smallest: 9, 7, 5, 3, 1, 0 gives 9,75,310.

qa.q: What is the smallest 6-digit number made with 4, 0, 2, 8, 6, 1 (each used once)?
qa.e: A number cannot start with 0, so start with 1, then 0, 2, 4, 6, 8: 1,02,468.

qa.q: A number is between 2,99,000 and 3,01,000. Its lakhs digit is 3. Which could it be?
qa.e: 3,00,500 has 3 lakhs and lies between 2,99,000 and 3,01,000. 3,01,500 and 3,10,000 are too big.

qa.q: Joseph says 89,999 is greater than 1,00,000 because 8 and 9 are big digits. What is the mistake?
qa.a: 1,00,000 has more digits, so it is greater
qa.e: First count digits. 1,00,000 has 6 digits and 89,999 has 5, so 1,00,000 is greater.

qa.q: Round 47 to the nearest ten.
qa.e: 47 is 3 away from 50 and 7 away from 40, so it rounds to 50.

qa.q: Round 82 to the nearest ten.
qa.e: The ones digit is 2, which is less than 5, so we round down to 80.

qa.q: Round 65 to the nearest ten.
qa.e: 65 is exactly halfway. Our rule says 5 or more rounds up, so 65 → 70.

qa.q: The rabbit is at 33. Food is at 30 and 40. How many hops of 1 to the nearer food?
qa.e: 30 is nearer: from 33 back to 30 is 3 hops.

qa.q: Round 5,678 to the nearest ten.
qa.e: Look at the ones digit 8. 8 ≥ 5, so round up: 5,678 → 5,680.

qa.q: Which number rounds to 90 to the nearest ten?
qa.e: 86 has ones digit 6, so it rounds up to 90. 84 → 80, 95 → 100, 79 → 80.

qa.q: Round 3,402 to the nearest ten.
qa.e: The ones digit is 2, less than 5, so round down to 3,400.

qa.q: Nisha has ₹74. To the nearest ten rupees, about how much does she have?
qa.e: The ones digit 4 is less than 5, so ₹74 is about ₹70.

qa.q: Round 470 to the nearest hundred.
qa.e: The tens digit is 7, which is 5 or more, so round up to 500.

qa.q: Round 6,239 to the nearest hundred.
qa.e: The tens digit is 3, less than 5, so round down to 6,200.

qa.q: Round 23,780 to the nearest thousand.
qa.e: The hundreds digit is 7, so round up: 23,780 → 24,000.

qa.q: Round 15,499 to the nearest thousand.
qa.e: The hundreds digit is 4, less than 5, so round down to 15,000. The 9s further right do not matter.

qa.q: A rounding table shows 3,756. What goes in the 'nearest 100' column?
qa.e: Tens digit is 5, so round up: 3,756 → 3,800.

qa.q: Round 9,650 to the nearest thousand.
qa.e: The hundreds digit is 6, so round up. 9,000 + 1,000 = 10,000.

qa.q: Which number rounds to 5,000 to the nearest thousand?
Round 2,086 to the nearest hundred.
qa.e: The tens digit is 8, so round up: 2,086 → 2,100.

qa.q: Which two numbers round to the same ten?
qa.e: 34 rounds down to 30 and 26 rounds up to 30.

qa.q: Which number rounds to 400 to the nearest hundred?
qa.e: 351 has tens digit 5, so it rounds up to 400. 349 → 300, 450 → 500, 460 → 500.

qa.q: Which number rounds to 2,000 both to the nearest hundred and to the nearest thousand?
qa.e: 2,010 → 2,000 (hundred) and 2,000 (thousand). 2,150 → 2,200 to the nearest hundred.

qa.q: What is the smallest number that rounds to 80 to the nearest ten?
qa.e: 75 is halfway, and 5 rounds up, so 75 → 80. 74 would round to 70.

qa.q: What is the biggest number that rounds to 600 to the nearest hundred?
qa.e: 649 has tens digit 4, so it rounds down to 600. 650 would round up to 700.

qa.q: Ria and Tara each think of a number that rounds to 5,000 to the nearest thousand. Which pair could they be?
qa.e: 4,700 rounds up to 5,000 and 5,300 rounds down to 5,000.

qa.q: Which number rounds to the same value at the ten, hundred and thousand levels?
qa.e: 9,000 is already a round thousand, so it stays 9,000 at all three levels.

qa.q: 4,567 is rounded at three levels. Which list is correct (ten, hundred, thousand)?
qa.e: Ones digit 7 → 4,570. Tens digit 6 → 4,600. Hundreds digit 5 → 5,000.

qa.q: Karan cycles 12 km every hour. How far does he go in 5 hours?
qa.e: Same distance each hour, so multiply: 12 × 5 = 60 km.

qa.q: A cyclist covers 18 km each hour. How long does she take to cover 90 km?
qa.e: 90 ÷ 18 = 5, so she needs 5 hours.

qa.q: 900 people must travel. Each bus has 45 seats. How many buses are needed?
qa.e: 900 ÷ 45 = 20 buses exactly.

qa.q: 130 children go on a trip. A van holds 12 children. How many vans are needed so everyone goes?
qa.e: 130 ÷ 12 = 10 vans with 10 children left over. Those 10 need one more van, so 11 vans.

qa.q: Which is the best way to estimate the number of leaves on a big neem tree?
qa.a: Count the leaves on one branch and multiply by the number of branches
qa.e: Counting a small part and multiplying gives a good estimate quickly.

qa.q: A notebook has 80 pages. Ravi writes about 120 words on each page. About how many words fit?
Which number is the most sensible estimate of people living in a big town?
qa.e: A big town has thousands of people, so 50,000 makes sense.

qa.q: One train coach carries about 80 people. About how many coaches carry 2,400 people?
A farmer must take a cat, a parrot and grain across a river. The boat holds him and one thing. The cat eats the parrot and the parrot eats the grain if left alone. Fewest crossings?
qa.e: Parrot over (1), back (2), cat over (3), parrot back (4), grain over (5), back (6), parrot over (7).

qa.q: Two adults and two children must cross. The boat carries one adult, or one or two children. Fewest crossings?
qa.e: Each adult needs 4 trips (2 children go, 1 returns, adult goes, other child returns). 4 + 4 = 8, then both children cross: 9.

qa.q: Pebble game: piles of 5 and 3. It is your turn. What should you do to leave equal piles?
qa.e: Taking 2 from 5 leaves 3 and 3, equal piles.

qa.q: In the pebble game, piles are 4 and 4 and it is your friend's turn. Your friend takes 3 from one pile. What do you do?
qa.e: Copying leaves 1 and 1. Then whatever your friend does, you take the last pebble.

qa.q: Reverse 85 and subtract the smaller from the bigger. What do you get?
For a 2-digit number, reverse-and-subtract gives 9 × (difference of the digits). What does 92 give?
qa.e: Digits 9 and 2 differ by 7. 9 × 7 = 63. Check: 92 − 29 = 63.

qa.q: Which number gives 0 when you reverse it and subtract?
qa.e: 44 reversed is still 44, and 44 − 44 = 0.

qa.q: Meena's reverse-and-subtract answer was 18. Which number could she have started with?
Which number lies between 34,560 and 34,570?
qa.e: 34,565 is bigger than 34,560 and smaller than 34,570.

qa.q: How many whole numbers are there between 20,100 and 20,105?
qa.e: They are 20,101, 20,102, 20,103, 20,104. That is 4 numbers.

qa.q: Delhi to Chennai by road is about 2,180 km. Delhi to Kolkata is about 1,530 km. How much farther is Chennai?
Which list of prices is in ascending order?
qa.e: Ascending means smallest first.

qa.q: Which number has a zero in the hundreds place?
qa.e: In 47,056 the hundreds digit is 0.

qa.q: Which number has zeros in both the ones and tens places?
qa.e: 56,300 ends in 00, so ones and tens are both 0.

qa.q: Town A has 38,905 people and Town B has 38,950. Which is true?
qa.e: 38,950 − 38,905 = 45, so Town B has 45 more.

qa.q: Write the largest 5-digit number with 0 in the thousands place.
qa.e: Put 9 everywhere except the thousands place: 90,999.

qa.q: 4,300 is how many hundreds?
qa.e: 4 thousands = 40 hundreds. 40 + 3 = 43 hundreds.

qa.q: Which is another way to write 6,800?
qa.e: 6 thousands = 60 hundreds, plus 8 hundreds = 68 hundreds.

qa.q: 2 thousands and 14 hundreds make which number?
Asha pays ₹4,000 using only ₹500 notes. How many notes does she use?
Rohit has 3 notes of ₹1,000, 2 notes of ₹500 and 6 notes of ₹10. How much money is that?
What is the fewest number of notes (₹1,000, ₹500, ₹100, ₹10) to make ₹1,620?
How many ₹10 notes make ₹1,000?
Which set of notes does NOT make ₹2,000?
qa.e: 3 × ₹500 = ₹1,500, not ₹2,000. The others all make ₹2,000.

qa.q: Plants are put around a square bed, 4 on each side including corners. How many plants are there?
qa.e: 4 × 4 = 16, but the 4 corner plants were counted twice. 16 − 4 = 12.

qa.q: Children stand around a square, 7 on each side including corners. How many children?
A king's guard adds 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36 horses around the palace. There are 3 horses in each corner room. What is his mistake?
qa.a: He counted each corner room twice
qa.e: Each corner room is on two sides, so it was counted twice.

qa.q: Rooms around a square palace: 4 corners and 4 middles. Each corner has 3 horses and each middle has 3. How many horses in all?
qa.e: 8 rooms × 3 = 24 horses. Each side still shows 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

qa.q: Same palace: now each corner has 4 horses and each middle has 1. How many horses does each side show?
qa.e: A side is corner + middle + corner = 4 + 1 + 4 = 9.

qa.q: With 4 horses in each corner and 1 in each middle, how many horses are there in all?
qa.e: Corners: 4 × 4 = 16. Middles: 4 × 1 = 4. Total 20 — fewer horses, but each side still shows 9!

qa.q: Lamps are put around a square, and the total is 20. How many lamps are on each side, counting corners?
Each side of a square shows 10 stones. Which total is NOT possible if every stone is on the edge?
qa.e: Each side shows 10, so the 4 sides add to 40. Stones in corners are counted twice, so the real total can be 40 or less, never more. 44 is impossible.

qa.q: A grid has 8 equal squares. How many squares show 1/8?
qa.e: 1/8 means 1 of 8 equal parts. With 8 squares, 1 square is one part.

qa.q: A grid has 12 squares. Ravi shades 2 of them. What fraction is shaded?
qa.e: 2 shaded out of 12 equal squares is 2/12.

qa.q: To shade 1/6 of a grid with 12 squares, how many squares must be shaded?
qa.e: 12 squares in 6 equal parts gives 2 squares in each part. Shade one part: 2 squares.

qa.q: A grid of 6 squares is in 3 columns of 2. One column is shaded. Which two names fit?
qa.e: One of 3 equal columns is 1/3. It is 2 of 6 small squares, so 2/6 too.

qa.q: Which fraction is the same shaded part as 1/3?
qa.e: Splitting each third into 2 gives 2 of 6 parts: 2/6 = 1/3.

qa.q: A 12-square grid has 3 squares shaded. Which other fraction names it?
qa.e: 12 squares in 4 equal parts has 3 squares in each part. 3 shaded = 1 part of 4 = 1/4.

qa.q: Ayaan says 4 shaded squares out of 8 is 1/4. What is right?
qa.e: 4 out of 8 is half of the grid, so 4/8 = 1/2.

qa.q: How many squares are there in a grid that shows 1/12 when 1 square is shaded?
qa.e: If 1 square is 1/12, there are 12 equal squares in all.

qa.q: How many 1/4 pieces make one whole strip?
qa.e: The whole is cut into 4 equal quarters, so 4 pieces make it.

qa.q: How many 1/4 pieces are as long as one 1/2 piece?
Tina has one 1/2 piece and one 1/4 piece. Which piece completes the whole?
Which set makes exactly one whole?
Raju has one 1/2 piece. How many 1/6 pieces does he need to finish the whole?
qa.e: 1/2 = 3/6. A whole is 6/6. 6/6 − 3/6 = 3/6, so three 1/6 pieces.

qa.q: How many 1/12 pieces make one whole?
qa.e: 12 twelfths make a whole: 12/12 = 1.

qa.q: Meera uses two 1/4 pieces and some 1/12 pieces to make a whole. How many 1/12 pieces?
Which set does NOT make one whole?
Which of these fractions equals one half?
qa.e: 4 is half of 8, so 4/8 = 1/2.

qa.q: 5/10 of a ribbon is cut. Is that half?
qa.e: 5 is half of 10, so 5/10 = 1/2.

qa.q: How many 1/8 pieces make 1/4?
qa.e: 1/4 = 2/8, so two 1/8 pieces.

qa.q: How many 1/6 pieces make 1/2?
qa.e: 1/2 = 3/6, so three 1/6 pieces.

qa.q: How many 1/12 pieces make 1/4?
qa.e: 1/4 = 3/12, so three 1/12 pieces.

qa.q: 6/? = 1/2. What number goes in the box?
qa.e: The bottom must be double the top. 6 × 2 = 12.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT equal to 1/2?
qa.e: Half of 7 is 3 1/2, not 3, so 3/7 is not 1/2.

qa.q: Kiran fits 1/8 pieces along a 1/2 piece. How many does she need?
qa.e: 1/2 = 4/8, so 4 eighths fit.

qa.q: Which fraction is equal to 1/2?
qa.e: 3/6 means 3 of 6 equal parts. That is half of the whole.

qa.q: A chikki bar has 8 equal pieces. Meena eats 2. What fraction did she eat, in simplest form?
qa.e: 2 of 8 is 2/8. Divide top and bottom by 2: 1/4.

qa.q: 3/4 = ?/12. What number goes in the box?
qa.e: 4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the top by 3 too: 3 × 3 = 9.

qa.q: Kabir says 2/3 = 4/9 because 2 × 2 = 4 and 3 × 3 = 9. Is he right?
qa.a: No, he must multiply top and bottom by the same number
qa.e: He used × 2 on top but × 3 at the bottom. 2/3 = 4/6 or 6/9, not 4/9.

qa.q: Which pair of fractions are equivalent?
qa.e: 2/5: multiply top and bottom by 2 → 4/10. Same amount.

qa.q: Harpreet folds a paper into 3 equal parts and colours 1 part. Then she folds each part in half. How many small parts are coloured now?
qa.e: The paper now has 6 small parts. The coloured third is now 2 small parts: 1/3 = 2/6.

qa.q: On a number line from 0 to 1, which fraction lands on the same spot as 1/2?
qa.e: 5/10 means 5 of 10 equal jumps, which is exactly halfway.

qa.q: 4/5 = 16/?. What number goes in the box?
qa.e: 4 × 4 = 16, so multiply the bottom by 4: 5 × 4 = 20.

qa.q: Write 6/8 in simplest form.
qa.e: Divide top and bottom by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, 8 ÷ 2 = 4.

qa.q: What is 10/15 in simplest form?
qa.e: Both 10 and 15 can be divided by 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 and 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

qa.q: What is 9/12 in simplest form?
qa.e: Both 9 and 12 can be divided by 3: 9/12 = 3/4.

qa.q: Aisha has 20 marbles. 15 are blue. What fraction is blue, in simplest form?
qa.e: 15 of 20 is 15/20. Divide top and bottom by 5: 3/4.

qa.q: Which fraction is already in simplest form?
qa.e: Only 1 divides both 5 and 7. The others can be divided by 2 or 3.

qa.q: Joseph divides the top of 8/12 by 4 and the bottom by 2, and gets 2/6. What went wrong?
qa.a: He must divide top and bottom by the same number
qa.e: 8/12 ÷ 4 on both gives 2/3. Using different numbers changes the amount.

qa.q: A box had 18 laddoos. 12 were eaten at a Diwali party. What fraction was eaten, in simplest form?
qa.e: 12/18. Divide both by 6: 2/3.

qa.q: To simplify 16/24 in one step, which is the biggest number that divides both 16 and 24?
qa.e: 8 divides 16 (2 times) and 24 (3 times). No bigger number divides both. 16/24 = 2/3.

qa.q: Are 2/3 and 8/12 equal?
Which sign goes in 3/8 ☐ 1/4?
Which sign goes in 5/12 ☐ 1/2?
Which sign goes in 4/6 ☐ 2/3?
qa.e: 2/3 = 4/6, so they are equal.

qa.q: Which fraction completes 3/5 = ?/10?
Which statement is true?
Sonu says 2/5 and 3/10 are equal. To check, he writes 2/5 with bottom 10. What does he get?
qa.e: 2/5 = 4/10, which is more than 3/10.

qa.q: Which is the right way to write 'one-sixth is less than one-third'?
qa.e: The < sign means 'is less than', with the smaller number on the left.

qa.q: Which is bigger: 3/7 or 5/7?
qa.e: The pieces are the same size (sevenths). 5 pieces are more than 3 pieces.

qa.q: Which is bigger: 1/3 or 1/5?
qa.e: Cutting into 3 gives bigger pieces than cutting into 5. So 1/3 > 1/5.

qa.q: Riya ate 2/3 of a dosa. Kabir ate 3/4 of the same size dosa. Who ate more?
qa.e: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12. 9/12 is more, so Kabir ate more.

qa.q: Which fraction is more than 1/2?
qa.e: Half of 8 is 4. 5/8 has 5 parts, more than 4, so it is more than half.

qa.q: Put 3/8, 1/2 and 1/4 in order from smallest. Which is in the middle?
qa.e: In eighths: 1/4 = 2/8, 3/8, 1/2 = 4/8. So 3/8 is in the middle.

qa.q: Meena drank 5/6 of a glass of lassi. Aisha drank 7/12 of the same glass. Who drank more?
qa.e: 5/6 = 10/12. 10/12 is more than 7/12, so Meena drank more.

qa.q: Which is the largest: 2/3, 3/5 or 1/2?
In a race, Arjun has run 3/10 of the track and Harpreet has run 2/5. Who is ahead?
qa.e: 2/5 = 4/10. 4/10 is more than 3/10, so Harpreet is ahead.

qa.q: Seven half-parathas were eaten. How many parathas is that?
qa.e: 2 halves make 1 paratha. 7 halves = 3 wholes and 1 half = 3 1/2.

qa.q: Mum cut apples into quarters. 12 quarters were used for chaat. How many whole apples?
qa.e: 4 quarters make 1 apple. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 apples.

qa.q: Write 11/4 as a mixed number.
qa.e: 11 ÷ 4 = 2 remainder 3, so 2 wholes and 3 quarters.

qa.q: Write 5/3 as a mixed number.
qa.e: 5 ÷ 3 = 1 remainder 2, so 1 2/3.

qa.q: Which fraction is the same as 2 1/2?
qa.e: 2 wholes = 4 halves, plus 1 half = 5 halves = 5/2.

qa.q: Rahul ate 3 halves of a roti and Ria ate 2 halves. How many rotis did they eat together?
qa.e: 3 halves + 2 halves = 5 halves = 2 1/2 rotis.

qa.q: How many quarters are there in 3 whole cakes?
qa.e: Each cake has 4 quarters. 3 × 4 = 12.

qa.q: Which is a fraction greater than 1?
qa.e: In 9/4 the top is bigger than the bottom, so it is more than one whole.

qa.q: Sixteen ants stand in a line. Each ant is 1/4 cm long. How long is the line?
qa.e: 16 × 1/4 = 16/4 = 4 cm. Every 4 ants make 1 cm.

qa.q: Between which two whole numbers does 7/4 lie?
qa.e: 7/4 = 1 3/4, so it lies between 1 and 2.

qa.q: Which fraction is equal to 1?
qa.e: When top and bottom are equal, the fraction is one whole.

qa.q: Which fraction is less than 1?
qa.e: 6 is less than 7, so 6/7 is less than a whole.

qa.q: A grasshopper makes 6 jumps of 1/2 m. How far does it go?
How many jumps of 1/3 reach 2 on the number line?
qa.e: 3 jumps of 1/3 reach 1, so 6 jumps reach 2.

qa.q: Which is the right order from left to right on a number line?
qa.e: Same bottom: bigger top is further right. 2 < 4 < 5.

qa.q: Riya walks 5 laps of 1/4 km. How far does she walk?
Which is greater: 5/4 or 7/8?
qa.e: 5/4 is more than 1, and 7/8 is less than 1. So 5/4 is greater.

qa.q: Which fraction is exactly half?
qa.e: 7 is exactly half of 14.

qa.q: Why is 3/8 less than 1/2?
qa.a: Half of 8 is 4, and 3 is less than 4
qa.e: For 1/2 the top would be 4. Since 3 < 4, 3/8 is less than half.

qa.q: Which fraction is less than 1/2?
qa.e: Half of 9 is 4 1/2. 4 < 4 1/2, so 4/9 is less than half.

qa.q: Using 1/2, compare 2/5 and 4/7.
qa.e: 2/5 is less than half (half of 5 is 2 1/2). 4/7 is more than half (half of 7 is 3 1/2). So 2/5 < 4/7.

qa.q: Which fraction is more than 1?
qa.e: In 10/9 the top is bigger than the bottom.

qa.q: Aman ate 3/7 of a cake and Lata ate 5/8 of the same size cake. Who ate more?
qa.e: 3/7 is less than half and 5/8 is more than half, so Lata ate more.

qa.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
qa.e: 2/9 is less than half, 1/2 is half, 7/6 is more than 1.

qa.q: How many degrees are there in a full turn?
qa.e: A full turn brings you back to where you started. It is 360°.

qa.q: A half turn is how many degrees?
qa.e: Half of a full turn: 360° ÷ 2 = 180°.

qa.q: Arjun faces North and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now?
qa.e: Clockwise from North the next direction is East. A quarter turn takes you there.

qa.q: How many quarter turns make one full turn?
qa.e: Each quarter turn is 90°. 360° ÷ 90° = 4.

qa.q: The minute hand moves from 12 to 3. How many degrees does it turn?
qa.e: 12 to 3 is a quarter of the clock: 3 gaps × 30° = 90°.

qa.q: Kabir makes a three-quarter turn. How many degrees is that?
qa.e: Three quarter turns: 3 × 90° = 270°.

qa.q: Meena faces East and makes a half turn. Which way does she face now?
qa.e: A half turn makes you face the opposite way. Opposite of East is West.

qa.q: The minute hand goes from 12 to 6. What kind of turn is this?
qa.e: 12 to 6 is halfway round the clock. That is a half turn, 180°.

qa.q: Which of these makes full turns again and again?
qa.e: Fan blades go round and round, making full turns.

qa.q: A clothes clip opens as wide as it can. Is the opening more or less than a quarter turn?
qa.e: A clip opens only a little — much less than a square corner.

qa.q: Which object can open to about a half turn, making a straight line?
qa.e: A notebook opened flat makes a straight line, a half turn.

qa.q: Which is NOT an example of turning?
qa.a: Sliding a book across a table
qa.e: Sliding moves something along without turning it.

qa.q: A cupboard door is opened so it makes a square corner with the cupboard. What turn is that?
qa.e: A square corner is a quarter turn.

qa.q: Raghav twists a bottle cap 3 full turns. Where does the mark on the cap point now?
qa.e: After each full turn the cap is back to where it started, so after 3 full turns it is the same.

qa.q: Which opens to more than a quarter turn?
qa.e: A laptop lid can open well past a square corner.

qa.q: Two half turns of a giant wheel make how much turn?
qa.e: Half + half = one full turn.

qa.q: What kind of angle is 45°?
qa.e: 45° is less than 90°, so it is acute.

qa.q: Which angle is obtuse?
qa.e: 150° is more than 90° and less than 180°.

qa.q: The corner of a notebook page makes which kind of angle?
qa.e: A page corner is a square corner, 90°. That is a right angle.

qa.q: What kind of angle is 179°?
qa.e: 179° is more than 90° and just less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

qa.q: At 3 o'clock, what kind of angle do the clock hands make?
qa.e: From 12 to 3 is 3 × 30° = 90°, a right angle.

qa.q: At 1 o'clock, what kind of angle do the clock hands make?
qa.e: From 12 to 1 is 30°, which is less than 90°. It is acute.

qa.q: At 5 o'clock, the smaller angle between the hands is 150°. What kind of angle is it?
qa.e: 150° is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.

qa.q: Harpreet says every angle bigger than 90° is obtuse. Is she right?
qa.a: No, an obtuse angle must also be less than 180°
qa.e: Obtuse angles are between 90° and 180°. 180° is a straight angle, so 'bigger than 90°' is not enough.

qa.q: Neha opens her paper fan just a little. What angle does it make?
qa.e: A small opening is less than a quarter turn, which is acute.

qa.q: She opens the fan wider, more than a square corner but not flat. What angle now?
qa.e: Between a quarter turn and a half turn is obtuse.

qa.q: In a house drawing, what angle is made where the wall meets the floor?
qa.e: Walls stand straight up from the floor, making a square corner.

qa.q: A drawn roof has a pointed top that is sharper than a square corner. What angle is the top?
qa.e: Sharper than a square corner means less than a right angle, so acute.

qa.q: A gymnast lifts one leg straight up while standing on the other. The legs look like an L. What angle is that?
qa.e: An L shape is a square corner, a right angle.

qa.q: Which body position shows a straight angle?
qa.a: Arms stretched out sideways in one line
qa.e: Arms stretched out in one line make a straight line, a half turn.

qa.q: A five-sided house shape has 2 right angles at the bottom and an acute angle at the top. What are the other 2 angles?
qa.e: The roof slopes out from the wall, making angles wider than a square corner: obtuse.

qa.q: Which shape can have 2 right, 2 obtuse and 1 acute angle?
qa.e: A pentagon like a house with a pointed roof has this mix. A square and rectangle have only right angles; a triangle has 3 angles.

qa.q: An arrow made a 1/2 turn and now points down. Which way did it start?
qa.e: A half turn makes it face the opposite way, so it started pointing up.

qa.q: An arrow made a 1/4 turn clockwise and now points right (to 3). Where did it start?
qa.e: Turn back a quarter turn anticlockwise from 3 to reach 12.

qa.q: An arrow turned 1/8 turn clockwise and now points to 3 o'clock. Where did it start?
qa.e: 1/8 turn is half of a quarter turn. Going back from 3 by half a quarter lands halfway between 12 and 3.

qa.q: How many 1/8 turns make a quarter turn?
qa.e: 1/4 = 2/8, so two eighth turns.

qa.q: 3/8 of a turn is between which two turns?
qa.a: A quarter turn and a half turn
qa.e: 1/4 = 2/8 and 1/2 = 4/8. 3/8 is between them.

qa.q: Which fraction of a turn is 4/8 the same as?
qa.e: 4/8 is half of 8 eighths, so it is a half turn.

qa.q: 5/8 of a full turn is how many degrees?
An arrow ends pointing left after a 1/2 turn. Where did it start?
qa.e: A half turn reverses the arrow, so it started pointing right.

qa.q: What fraction of a full turn is 1/2 + 1/4 turn?
What fraction of a full turn is 1/4 + 1/8 turn?
Sunil measures an angle with his turn measurer. It covers 3 of the 8 equal parts. What kind of angle is it?
qa.e: 3/8 is more than 2/8 (a quarter) but less than 4/8 (a half), so obtuse.

qa.q: An angle covers exactly 2 of the 8 parts. What is it?
qa.e: 2/8 = 1/4 turn, which is a right angle.

qa.q: Jaya guesses an angle is a 1/4 turn. She measures and finds it is 1/8 turn. What kind of angle is it really?
qa.e: 1/8 turn is less than a quarter turn, so acute.

qa.q: How many degrees is a 3/4 turn?
Which is the best way to check your guess of an angle?
qa.a: Put the centre of the turn measurer on the corner and count the eighths
qa.e: Angle size is the amount of turn between the arms, not their length.

qa.q: 1/2 + 1/8 turn is the same as how many eighths?
Meera draws a turn of 1/8 and then 1/6 more. A 1/8 turn is 45° and a 1/6 turn is 60°. How big is the whole turn?
qa.e: 45° + 60° = 105°. That is more than a quarter turn (90°) and less than a half turn, so it is obtuse.

qa.q: On a clock face, how many degrees is the turn from one number to the next?
qa.e: A full turn is 360° and there are 12 gaps. 360° ÷ 12 = 30°.

qa.q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 2 o'clock?
qa.e: From 12 to 2 is 2 gaps: 2 × 30° = 60°.

qa.q: What is the angle between the clock hands at 6 o'clock?
qa.e: From 12 to 6 is 6 gaps: 6 × 30° = 180°. The hands make a straight line.

qa.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from 12 to 9. How many degrees does it turn?
qa.e: 12 to 9 clockwise is 9 gaps: 9 × 30° = 270°, a three-quarter turn.

qa.q: Which capital letter has a right angle?
qa.e: L has a straight up line meeting a flat line, making a square corner.

qa.q: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
qa.e: Every corner of a rectangle is a square corner, and it has 4 corners.

qa.q: In 20 minutes, through how many degrees does the minute hand turn?
qa.e: 20 minutes is 4 gaps of 5 minutes. 4 × 30° = 120°.

qa.q: Joseph opens a book flat so the two covers make a straight line. What is the angle between them?
qa.e: A straight line is a half turn, which is 180°.

qa.q: The minute hand points to 2. It makes a quarter turn. Where does it point now?
qa.e: A quarter turn is 15 minutes, which is 3 numbers. 2 + 3 = 5.

qa.q: The minute hand points to 1. It makes a half turn. Where does it point now?
qa.e: A half turn is 6 numbers. 1 + 6 = 7.

qa.q: The minute hand points to 10. It makes a quarter turn. Where does it point now?
qa.e: 10 + 3 = 13, but the clock goes back to 1 after 12.

qa.q: The minute hand starts at 12 and makes a three-quarter turn. Where does it point?
qa.e: Three-quarter turn = 45 minutes = 9 numbers. It lands on 9.

qa.q: Which way do the hands of a clock turn?
qa.e: Clockwise is named after the way clock hands move.

qa.q: A lizard faces up (north on the wall) and makes a quarter turn. Now it faces left. Which way did it turn?
qa.e: From up, turning to the left is opposite to clock hands, so anticlockwise.

qa.q: A ladybird faces right and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does it face now?
qa.e: Clockwise goes up → right → down → left. From right, the next is down.

qa.q: A bird faces down and makes a quarter turn. Now it faces right. Which way did it turn?
qa.e: Clockwise from down would go to left. Going to right is anticlockwise.

qa.q: Ravi faces North and makes 2 quarter turns clockwise. Which way does he face?
qa.e: Two quarter turns make a half turn, so he faces the opposite way: South.

qa.q: Meena faces West and makes 1 quarter turn clockwise. Which way does she face?
qa.e: Clockwise order: West → North.

qa.q: Ali faces South and makes 3 quarter turns clockwise. Which way does he face?
qa.e: Clockwise from South: West (1), North (2), East (3).

qa.q: Which turn makes you face the same way as 3 quarter turns clockwise?
qa.e: 3 quarter turns one way leave just 1 quarter turn to complete the circle, so it equals 1 quarter turn the other way.

qa.q: Sara faces East. She turns right, then right again. Which way does she face?
qa.e: Each right turn is a quarter clockwise: East → South → West.

qa.q: Raj faces North. After some turns he faces East. Which could NOT be his turn?
qa.e: A half turn from North gives South, not East. The others end at East.

qa.q: On a map, Asha faces the market, which is to her North. She makes a half turn. What is in front of her now?
qa.e: A half turn makes her face the opposite direction, South.

qa.q: Dev faces West. How many quarter turns anticlockwise make him face North?
qa.e: Anticlockwise from West: South (1), East (2), North (3).

qa.q: Group A is 8, 3, 5 and Group B is 2, 6, 4. What should each group's sum be after swapping?
qa.e: A = 16 and B = 12. Total 28, so each needs 28 ÷ 2 = 14.

qa.q: Group A is 8, 3, 5 and Group B is 2, 6, 4. Which one swap makes the sums equal?
qa.e: A must lose 2, and 8 − 6 = 2. Now A = 6 + 3 + 5 = 14 and B = 2 + 8 + 4 = 14.

qa.q: Two groups have sums 23 and 17. A swap moves x − y from the bigger group. What should x − y be?
qa.e: The difference is 23 − 17 = 6. Half of 6 is 3. Moving 3 makes both 20.

qa.q: Group A: 10, 3. Group B: 8, 1. Which swap makes the sums equal?
qa.e: A = 13, B = 9, each needs 11, so A must lose 2. 10 − 8 = 2 works. (Swapping 3 and 1 also works, but it is not listed.)

qa.q: Group A: 7, 6, 5. Group B: 4, 3, 1. What is the fewest number of swaps that makes the sums equal?
qa.e: A = 18, B = 8, each needs 13. A must lose 5. Swap 6 with 1: 6 − 1 = 5. One swap is enough.

qa.q: Group A: 9, 2. Group B: 5, 4. Which single swap makes the sums equal?
qa.e: A = 11, B = 9, so A must lose 1. The swaps move 9 − 5 = 4, 9 − 4 = 5, or make A bigger. None moves exactly 1.

qa.q: After a swap, Group A went from 20 to 17. Group B was 14. What is Group B now?
qa.e: Whatever A loses, B gains. A lost 3, so B is 14 + 3 = 17.

qa.q: Group A: 12, 5, 1 (sum 18). Group B: 7, 4, 3 (sum 14). Which swap makes the sums equal?
qa.e: Each group needs 16, so A must lose 2. 5 − 3 = 2. Now A = 12 + 3 + 1 = 16 and B = 7 + 4 + 5 = 16.

qa.q: What is 456 + 99?
qa.e: 456 + 100 = 556, then take away 1: 555.

qa.q: What is the easy way to work out 2,345 + 999?
qa.e: 999 is 1 less than 1,000, so add 1,000 and take away 1.

qa.q: Using 68 + 30, what is 68 + 29?
A bus tank has 48 litres of diesel. The driver fills 37 litres more. How much is in the tank?
A car used 18 L of petrol on Monday, 26 L on Tuesday and 24 L on Wednesday. How much in all?
Which is the same as 345 + 97?
One fuel tanker carries 2,500 L and another carries 1,999 L. How much do they carry together?
From 345 + 128 = 473, which subtraction fact is true?
qa.e: Take away one part from the total to get the other part.

qa.q: From 63 − 27 = 36, which addition fact is true?
qa.e: Add back what was taken away to get the start number.

qa.q: ? − 245 = 380. What is the missing number?
qa.e: Undo the subtraction by adding: 380 + 245 = 625.

qa.q: 512 − ? = 287. What is the missing number?
? + 1,450 = 3,000. What is the missing number?
Which operation undoes addition?
qa.e: Subtraction takes away what was added, so it undoes addition.

qa.q: Which is NOT in the fact family of 56 + 44 = 100?
qa.e: 56 − 44 is 12, not 100. The other three use the same three numbers correctly.

qa.q: Ravi had some marbles. He gave away 38 and has 47 left. How many did he have at first?
Which of these are consecutive numbers?
qa.e: 34, 35, 36 follow one after another with nothing skipped.

qa.q: The sum of two consecutive numbers is always…
qa.e: One number is odd and the other is even, and odd + even = odd.

qa.q: What is 15 + 16 + 17?
qa.e: Middle number 16 × 3 numbers = 48.

qa.q: Is the sum of 4 consecutive numbers odd or even?
qa.e: 4 consecutive numbers have 2 odd and 2 even numbers. Two odds make an even, so the total is even. Example: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.

qa.q: Which is true about the sum of 3 consecutive numbers?
qa.a: It can be odd or even
qa.e: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 is even, but 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 is odd.

qa.q: 1 + 2 = 3, 2 + 3 = 5, 3 + 4 = 7, 4 + 5 = 9. By how much does each sum grow?
qa.e: 3, 5, 7, 9 go up by 2 each time.
The sums grow by 3 each time: 12 + 3 = 15.

qa.q: Find 41 + 42 + 43 + 44 + 45 + 46 + 47 using the middle number.
qa.e: 7 numbers, middle is 44. 44 × 7 = 308.

qa.q: Riya's school collected ₹12,450 on Monday and ₹8,675 on Tuesday for a fair. How much in all?
qa.e: 12,450 + 8,675 = 21,125. Remember to carry in the tens, hundreds and thousands.

qa.q: A train has 1,248 passengers. 379 get off at Bhopal. How many are still on the train?
Kabir's town has 45,320 people. The next town has 38,905. How many more people live in Kabir's town?
qa.e: 'How many more' means subtract: 45,320 − 38,905 = 6,415.

qa.q: What is 50,000 − 1?
qa.e: One less than 50,000 is 49,999. All the zeros become 9s after borrowing.

qa.q: 26,500 + ? = 40,000. What is the missing number?
qa.e: Find the missing part by subtracting: 40,000 − 26,500 = 13,500.

qa.q: Meena's family drove 1,285 km to Jaipur, then 642 km to Agra, then 1,073 km back home. How far did they drive in all?
Arjun had ₹5,000. He spent ₹1,750 on books and ₹865 on shoes. How much money is left?
Aisha worked out 63,210 − 27,480 = 35,730. What is the best way to check her answer?
qa.a: Add 35,730 + 27,480 and see if you get 63,210
qa.e: Adding the answer to the number taken away should give back the starting number. 35,730 + 27,480 = 63,210, so she is right.

qa.q: Riya had ₹3,500. She spent ₹1,280 on a school bag and then got ₹750 from her nani on Raksha Bandhan. How much does she have now?
qa.e: Spending takes money away and receiving adds it: 3,500 − 1,280 = 2,220, then 2,220 + 750 = 2,970.

qa.q: Which two numbers from 2,345; 4,780; 5,620; 3,150 have a sum closest to 8,000?
Which two numbers from 6,250; 3,480; 4,100; 5,890 have a sum closest to 10,000?
A truck can carry 10,000 kg. It already has 6,450 kg. How much more can it carry?
A lorry carries 8,500 kg of cement. It drops 2,750 kg at one site and 3,125 kg at another. How much is left?
A boat can carry 1,500 kg. The passengers weigh 980 kg and their bags 365 kg. How much more can it carry?
A lift can carry 680 kg. People inside weigh 545 kg. Can a 150 kg trolley go in too?
qa.a: No, it would be 15 kg too much
qa.e: 545 + 150 = 695, which is 15 kg more than 680.

qa.q: Which pair from 2,480; 2,610; 1,995; 3,050 has a sum closest to 5,000?
A goods wagon can carry 25,000 kg. It has 12,600 kg of rice and 9,850 kg of wheat. How much space is left?
Round 3,462 to the nearest hundred.
qa.e: The tens digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up to 3,500.

qa.q: Round 67,280 to the nearest thousand.
qa.e: The hundreds digit is 2, less than 5, so round down to 67,000.

qa.q: Estimate 498 + 307 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
qa.e: 498 is about 500 and 307 is about 300. 500 + 300 = 800.

qa.q: A train carried 3,890 people on Monday and 5,120 on Tuesday. Rounding to the nearest thousand, about how many in all?
Riya has ₹1,000. She wants toys costing ₹212, ₹395 and ₹289. Round each to the nearest hundred. Does she have enough?
Which number rounds to 5,000 when rounded to the nearest thousand?
qa.e: 4,725 has hundreds digit 7, so it rounds up to 5,000. 4,450 rounds to 4,000; 5,620 and 5,501 round to 6,000.

qa.q: Estimate 612 − 289 by rounding each number to the nearest hundred.
qa.e: 612 is about 600 and 289 is about 300. 600 − 300 = 300.

qa.q: A school needs 28 buses with 52 seats each. Round both to the nearest ten to estimate the seats.
qa.e: 28 is about 30 and 52 is about 50. 30 × 50 = 1,500.

qa.q: Riya's estimate said ₹1,000 is enough for toys of ₹212, ₹395 and ₹289. She now adds exactly. How much money will be left?
qa.e: Exact total: 212 + 395 + 289 = 896. ₹1,000 is enough, and 1,000 − 896 = ₹104 is left.

qa.q: What must be added to 638 to make 1,000?
4,725 + ? = 10,000. What is the missing number?
73 + ? = 100. What is the missing number?
What is 562 − 99?
What is 845 − 9?
What is the easy way to work out 1,234 − 99?
qa.e: 99 is 1 less than 100. Taking away 100 takes away 1 too many, so add 1 back.

qa.q: 457 − ? = 99. What number must be taken away?
503 − ? = 9. What is the missing number?
Which number is a palindrome?
qa.e: 4,554 reads 4-5-5-4 both ways.

qa.q: How many palindromes are there between 10 and 100?
How many palindromes are there between 100 and 200?
What is the smallest 3-digit palindrome?
qa.e: 100 backwards is 001, so it is not a palindrome. 101 is.

qa.q: What is the next palindrome after 1,221?
qa.e: 4-digit palindromes look like abba. After 1,221 comes 1,331.

qa.q: In a 3 × 3 grid of 1 to 9 where rows grow left to right and columns grow top to bottom, where must 1 go?
qa.e: 1 is the smallest, so nothing can be to its left or above it.

qa.q: In the same growing grid, where must 9 go?
qa.e: 9 is the biggest, so it must be last in its row and its column.

qa.q: Which number is NOT a palindrome?
qa.e: 1,231 backwards is 1,321, which is different.

qa.q: Is 3,457 odd or even?
qa.e: The ones digit is 7, which is odd.

qa.q: Which number is even?
qa.e: 5,678 ends in 8, an even digit.

qa.q: 27 children stand in pairs. How many are left without a partner?
qa.e: 27 is odd. 13 pairs make 26, and 1 child is left.

qa.q: Without adding, is 135 + 247 odd or even?
qa.e: Both numbers are odd, and odd + odd = even.

qa.q: Without adding, is 246 + 135 odd or even?
qa.e: 246 is even and 135 is odd. Even + odd = odd.

qa.q: Start at 51 and keep adding 2. Which number can you land on?
qa.e: 51 is odd, and adding 2 keeps it odd. 75 is the only odd choice.

qa.q: Which sum is odd?
qa.e: 23 is odd and 40 is even. Odd + even = odd.

qa.q: Why can 36 laddoos be put into pairs with none left?
qa.e: Even numbers split into pairs exactly: 18 pairs.

qa.q: In how many ways can you make ₹6 using ₹1, ₹2 and ₹5 coins?
What is the fewest number of coins (₹1, ₹2, ₹5) to make ₹13?
qa.e: 5 + 5 + 2 + 1 = 13 uses 4 coins.

qa.q: A light starts off. Its switch is pressed 15 times. Is it on or off?
qa.e: Each press changes it. 15 is odd, so it ends opposite to the start: on.

qa.q: A fan starts off. Its switch is pressed 20 times. Is it on or off?
qa.e: 20 is even, so it ends the way it started: off.

qa.q: Everest is 8,849 m and K2 is 8,611 m. How much higher is Everest?
Kangchenjunga is 8,586 m and Nanda Devi is 7,816 m. What is the difference?
Heights: Everest 8,849 m, K2 8,611 m, Kangchenjunga 8,586 m. Which two are closest in height?
qa.e: 8,611 − 8,586 = 25 m, the smallest difference.

qa.q: A climber reached a peak in 2018, after her 26th birthday that year. In which year was she born?
350 certificates were printed but 412 children took part. How many more certificates are needed?
qa.e: 412 − 350 = 62 more are needed. This is a shortage.

qa.q: 600 badges were made for 548 children. How many badges are extra?
qa.e: 600 − 548 = 52 extra badges. This is a surplus.

qa.q: Asha saved ₹1,250 in January, ₹980 in February and ₹1,475 in March. How much did she save?
A factory made 12,450 toys on Monday and 9,875 on Tuesday. How many more on Monday?
Team A scored 287 runs and Team B scored 249. By how many runs did Team A win?
A factory must make 50,000 shirts. It has made 36,780. How many are still to be made?

qa.e: Add place by place, carrying: 74,120.

qa.q: A train ticket costs ₹1,245. What is the cost of 6 tickets?
qa.e: 1,245 × 6 = 7,470. Multiply each place by 6 and carry.

qa.q: What is 48 × 100?
qa.e: Multiplying by 100 puts two zeros at the end: 4,800.

qa.q: 1,350 students go on a trip in buses. Each bus takes 45 students. How many buses are needed?
A plane flies 850 km every hour. How far does it fly in 12 hours?
Harpreet shares 2,400 packets of rangoli colours equally among 8 shops. How many packets does each shop get?
What is 236 × 25?
Joseph packs 97 laddoos in boxes of 8. How many full boxes does he get, and how many laddoos are left?
qa.e: 8 × 12 = 96, so 12 full boxes. 97 − 96 = 1 laddoo is left.

qa.q: A cricket stadium sold 3,250 tickets each day for 4 days. How many tickets were sold in all?
Which unit is best for measuring the length of a pencil?
qa.e: A pencil is short, so centimetres fit best.

qa.q: Which unit is best for the distance from Delhi to Agra?
qa.e: Towns are far apart, so we use kilometres.

qa.q: An eraser lies on a ruler. It starts at the 2 cm mark and ends at the 7 cm mark. How long is it?
qa.e: Length = end − start = 7 − 2 = 5 cm.

qa.q: Which unit should Meena use to measure the length of her classroom?
qa.e: A classroom is a few metres long, so metres fit best.

qa.q: Kabir takes 10 steps. Each step is about 50 cm. About how far does he walk?
Meena's school is 2 km from home. She walks there and back every day. How far does she walk each day?
qa.e: There and back is the distance two times: 2 km + 2 km = 4 km.

qa.q: How many millimetres make 1 centimetre?
qa.e: Look at a ruler: each centimetre has 10 small marks. 1 cm = 10 mm.

qa.q: Which road is the longest?
qa.e: 1 km = 1,000 m, which is more than 900 m. 1,500 cm is only 15 m.

qa.q: How many centimetres are there in 3 m?
6 km = ? m
Write 4 m 8 cm in centimetres.
Write 2,750 m in km and m.
Riya's saree is 550 cm long. How long is it in metres and centimetres?
Aisha ran 1 km 200 m. Joseph ran 1,020 m. Who ran farther?
qa.e: 1 km 200 m = 1,200 m. 1,200 m is more than 1,020 m.

qa.q: Half a kilometre is how many metres?
Kabir cuts a 3 m ribbon into pieces of 25 cm for rakhis. How many pieces does he get?
On a double number line, which centimetre mark sits below 4 m?
qa.e: Each metre is 100 cm, so 4 m lines up with 4 × 100 = 400 cm.

qa.q: On a double number line, a mark is halfway between 2 m and 3 m. What is it in cm?
qa.e: Halfway between 200 cm and 300 cm is 250 cm.

qa.q: The Statue of Unity is about 182 m tall. A temple tower is 66 m tall. How much taller is the statue?
Statue P is 45 m tall, statue Q is 4,050 cm and statue R is 42 m 60 cm. Which is the tallest?
qa.e: In cm: P = 4,500 cm, Q = 4,050 cm, R = 4,260 cm. P is the tallest.

qa.q: A palm tree is 9 m 40 cm tall and a neem tree is 7 m 85 cm. What is the difference?
Which length, doubled, gives 3 m?
qa.e: 3 m = 300 cm. Half of 300 cm is 150 cm = 1 m 50 cm.

qa.q: Rani's height is 1 m 20 cm. Her father is double her height. How tall is he?
Which length doubled gives 1 m 70 cm?
Mira takes 200 steps to walk 100 m. How many steps does she take for 300 m?
qa.e: 100 m takes 200 steps, so 300 m takes 3 × 200 = 600 steps.

qa.q: Arjun takes 200 steps in 100 m. About how long is one step?
With 2 steps for every metre, about how far is a shop that is 900 steps away?
qa.e: 2 steps = 1 m, so 900 steps = 900 ÷ 2 = 450 m.

qa.q: Which place is nearest to school: library 750 m, bank 1 km 5 m, clinic 1,050 m?
qa.e: In metres: 750, 1,005 and 1,050. 750 is the smallest.

qa.q: Which place is farthest: playground 1 km 200 m, lake 1,020 m, fort 1 km 80 m?
qa.e: In metres: 1,200, 1,020 and 1,080. The playground is farthest.

qa.q: Tina measures 200 m with a tape. Why does she count her steps over it?
qa.a: To know about how many steps she takes for a known distance
qa.e: Knowing steps for a known distance lets her estimate other distances.

qa.q: Raj takes 140 steps for 100 m. His uncle takes 120 steps for 100 m. Who has the longer step?
qa.e: Fewer steps for the same distance means each step is longer.

qa.q: Put in order from nearest: A 2 km, B 1,800 m, C 2 km 50 m. Which is in the middle?
qa.e: 1,800 m < 2,000 m < 2,050 m. A (2 km) is in the middle.

qa.q: A train goes from Rampur to Sitapur (64 km) and then from Sitapur to Gopalpur (96 km). How far is Rampur to Gopalpur on this route?
qa.e: Add the two parts: 64 + 96 = 160 km.

qa.q: Meena walked 1 km 250 m in the morning and 850 m in the evening. How many metres did she walk in all?
Arjun's school is 2 km from home. He has cycled 1 km 350 m. How much farther must he go?
Which is shorter: 3 km 40 m or 3,400 m?
qa.e: 3 km 40 m = 3,040 m, and 3,040 m is less than 3,400 m.

qa.q: One lap of a running track is 400 m. How many laps make 2 km?
Kabir's home is 750 m from the cycle shop. He goes to the shop and back home two times in a day. How far does he travel?
qa.e: Each round trip is 750 × 2 = 1,500 m. Two round trips: 3,000 m = 3 km.

qa.q: Riya has 5 m of lace. She uses 1 m 75 cm to decorate a diya stand. How much lace is left?
A road sign says 'Jaipur 48 km'. Later another sign says 'Jaipur 19 km'. How far has the car gone between the signs?
A 3 km route has a marker every 500 m, including the start and finish. How many markers?
How many gaps of 300 m are in 3 km?
A 3 km route has markers every 50 m, including both ends. How many markers?
A 2 km path has a bench every 250 m, including both ends. How many benches?
qa.e: 2,000 ÷ 250 = 8 gaps, so 8 + 1 = 9 benches.

qa.q: A race track has 11 markers at equal gaps of 100 m from start to finish. How long is it?
qa.e: 11 markers make 10 gaps. 10 × 100 m = 1,000 m = 1 km.

qa.q: Volunteers stand every 200 m on a 1 km route, but not at the start. How many volunteers?
qa.e: 1,000 ÷ 200 = 5 gaps. No one at the start, so 5 volunteers (at 200, 400, 600, 800, 1,000 m).

qa.q: Flags are placed at 0 m, 400 m, 800 m … up to 2 km. How many flags?
qa.e: 2,000 ÷ 400 = 5 gaps, so 6 flags.

qa.q: Why is the number of markers one more than the number of gaps?
qa.a: Because there is a marker at the start as well as at the end of each gap
qa.e: Each gap ends at a marker, and one more marker stands at the very start.

qa.q: Table (distance from Amgaon): Bhimpur 312 km, Chandanpur 1,045 km. How far is Bhimpur from Chandanpur?
Chandanpur is 1,045 km and Devgarh is 2,380 km from Amgaon. How far apart are they?
Devgarh is 2,380 km and Ekpur 4,189 km from Amgaon. How far from Devgarh to Ekpur?
In the table, what does 'Bhimpur 312 km' mean?
qa.a: Bhimpur is 312 km from the first station, Amgaon
qa.e: The table shows distance from the starting station.

qa.q: Table: Bhimpur 312 km, Chandanpur 1,045 km, Devgarh 2,380 km from Amgaon. Which station is 1,045 km from Amgaon?
qa.e: Read along the table: the row with 1,045 km is Chandanpur.

qa.q: Which part is longest: Amgaon–Bhimpur (312 km), Bhimpur–Chandanpur (733 km) or Chandanpur–Devgarh (1,335 km)?
qa.e: 1,335 km is the biggest of the three.

qa.q: Riya travels from Bhimpur (312 km) to Devgarh (2,380 km). How far does she go?
Is Bhimpur–Chandanpur (733 km) longer or shorter than Devgarh–Ekpur (1,809 km)? By how much?
qa.e: 1,809 − 733 = 1,076, so it is 1,076 km shorter.

qa.q: How many millimetres are there in 7 cm?
