qa.e: 1 cm = 10 mm, so 7 cm = 70 mm.

qa.q: A pencil lead line ends 4 small marks after the 6 cm mark (starting at 0). How long is it?
qa.e: 6 cm and 4 small mm marks: 6 cm 4 mm.

qa.q: A seed sprout was 3 mm on Day 1 and 12 mm on Day 4. How much did it grow?
Write 4 cm 5 mm in millimetres.
qa.e: 4 cm = 40 mm, plus 5 mm = 45 mm.

qa.q: An eraser starts at the 2 cm mark and ends at 5 cm 6 mm. How long is it?
qa.e: 56 mm − 20 mm = 36 mm = 3 cm 6 mm.

qa.q: To draw a line 38 mm long, where should Ravi stop his pencil?
qa.a: At the 8th small mark after 3 cm
qa.e: 38 mm = 3 cm 8 mm.

qa.q: Which is the best unit to measure the thickness of a coin?
qa.e: A coin is only about 1–2 mm thick, so mm is best.

qa.q: A bean sprout grows 2 mm every day. How long will it be after 6 days, if it starts at 5 mm?
qa.e: Growth 6 × 2 = 12 mm. 5 + 12 = 17 mm.

qa.q: Write 47 mm in cm and mm.
qa.e: 47 ÷ 10 = 4 remainder 7, so 4 cm 7 mm.

qa.q: Write 8 cm 2 mm in mm.
qa.e: 8 cm = 80 mm, plus 2 mm = 82 mm.

qa.q: Simran joins ribbons of 2 m 75 cm and 1 m 50 cm. How long is the ribbon now?
Kabir has 1 m 65 cm of rope and buys 85 cm more. How much rope does he have?
Which is longer: 2 km 80 m or 2,600 m?
qa.e: 2 km 80 m = 2,080 m, which is less than 2,600 m.

qa.q: How much longer is 2,600 m than 2 km 80 m?
Which is bigger: 5 m 6 cm or 560 cm? What is the difference?
A strip of 9 cm 6 mm and one of 3 cm 8 mm are joined. How long is the joined strip in mm?
What is 3 m 25 cm × 4?
5 m of cloth costs ₹450. What does 1 m cost?
1 m of ribbon costs ₹35. What do 6 m cost?
4 curtains each need 2 m 25 cm of cloth. How much cloth in all?
That 9 m of curtain cloth costs ₹80 a metre. What is the total cost?
A 12 km 600 m road is shared equally among 3 teams. How much does each team build?
3 m of lace costs ₹150. Using a double number line, what do 7 m cost?
A 5 km 500 m walking track is split into 5 equal parts. How long is each part?
A building has 6 floors. Each floor is about 3 m high. About how tall is it?
About how tall is a 2-floor house?
qa.e: Each floor is about 3 m, so 2 floors make about 6 m.

qa.q: A well is as deep as 4 ropes of 2 m each. How deep is it?
How many inches make 1 foot?
qa.e: 1 foot = 12 inches.

qa.q: 1 inch is about how long?
qa.e: 1 inch is about 2 cm 5 mm (25 mm).

qa.q: Megha is 4 feet 5 inches tall. How many inches is that?
qa.e: 4 × 12 = 48 inches, plus 5 = 53 inches.

qa.q: A table is 3 feet long. About how many cm is that?
qa.e: 1 foot is about 30 cm, so 3 feet is about 90 cm.

qa.q: Raju is 4 feet 8 inches and Sunil is 4 feet 11 inches. Who is taller, and by how much?
qa.e: Both are 4 feet. 11 − 8 = 3, so Sunil is 3 inches taller.

qa.q: ○ × 6 = 54. What number is ○?
Using 3, 4 and 5 once each in ☐☐ × ☐, which gives the biggest product?
qa.e: 43 × 5 = 215 beats 53 × 4 = 212 and 54 × 3 = 162. Putting the biggest digit as the single multiplier helps here.

qa.q: Using 3, 4 and 5 once each in ☐☐ × ☐, which product is closest to 200?
qa.e: 212 is 12 away from 200. 215 is 15 away, 170 is 30 away.

qa.q: A hall has 14 rows with 16 chairs in each row. How many chairs?
A box of laddoos has 4 layers. Each layer has 5 rows of 6 laddoos. How many laddoos?
qa.e: One layer: 5 × 6 = 30. Four layers: 30 × 4 = 120.

qa.q: A garden has 9 rows of 12 rose plants, but 4 plants are missing. How many plants are there?
I am odd, between 30 and 40, and in the 7 times table. Who am I?
qa.e: 7-table numbers between 30 and 40: 35 only. It is odd too.

qa.q: I am a multiple of 5 between 20 and 40. I am even. My tens digit is 3. Who am I?
qa.e: Multiples of 5 between 20 and 40: 25, 30, 35. Even: 30. Tens digit 3: 30.

qa.q: Clues: (A) I am less than 50. (B) I am in the 10 times table. (C) I am more than 30. (D) I am a 2-digit number. Which clue is not needed?
qa.e: A, B and C already give only 40. Every number from them is 2-digit anyway, so D adds nothing.

qa.q: I am a 2-digit number. I am in both the 4 and 6 times tables. I am less than 20. Who am I?
qa.e: In both tables and less than 20: 12 only.

qa.q: Using 6 and 3 with one operation, which number can you NOT make?
Which uses two numbers and one operation to make 0?
Which pair with one operation makes 17?
Riya makes 20 using 4 and a mystery number with ×. What is the mystery number?
Which is the same as 18 × 7?
qa.e: Changing the order of the factors gives the same product.

qa.q: What is 2,457 × 0?
qa.e: Any number times 0 is 0.

qa.q: What is 45 × 10?
qa.e: Each digit moves one place to the left: 45 → 450.

qa.q: What is 63 × 1,000?
qa.e: × 1,000 moves the digits three places left: 63,000.

qa.q: What is 60 × 50?
qa.e: 6 × 5 = 30, and there are two zeros: 3,000.

qa.q: What is 40 × 500?
qa.e: 4 × 5 = 20, then three zeros: 20,000.

qa.q: In a place-value chart, 342 × 100 moves the 3 from the hundreds place to which place?
qa.e: × 100 moves each digit two places left: hundreds → thousands → ten thousands. 342 × 100 = 34,200.

qa.q: A carton holds 80 milk packets. How many packets are in 30 cartons?
qa.e: 8 × 3 = 24, then two zeros: 2,400.

qa.q: Which is equal to 16 × 25?
qa.e: Halve 16 to 8 and double 25 to 50. The product stays 400.

qa.q: What is 48 × 5?
qa.e: 48 × 10 = 480, and half of that is 240.

qa.q: What is 36 × 25?
Which product is made easier by doubling and halving?
qa.e: 14 × 15 = 7 × 30, which is easy. The others have no handy half or double.

qa.q: Ravi halves 18 and doubles 35. Which product does he get?
qa.e: Half of 18 is 9 and double 35 is 70.

qa.q: What is 9 × 70, the same as 18 × 35?
qa.e: 9 × 7 = 63, add a zero: 630.

qa.q: Meena buys 25 packets of chikki at ₹28 each. What is the cost?
What is 126 × 5?
What is 7 × 29?
qa.e: 7 × 30 = 210. 29 is one less than 30, so take away one 7: 203.

qa.q: What is 8 × 99?
qa.e: 8 × 100 = 800, then take away 8: 792.

qa.q: What is 6 × 51?
qa.e: 6 × 50 = 300, then add one 6: 306.

qa.q: Which is the right way to find 9 × 48?
What is 5 × 198?
4 notebooks cost ₹99 each. What is the total?
For which product is the nearest-multiple method most useful?
qa.e: 99 is just 1 away from 100, so 6 × 99 = 600 − 6 is quick.

qa.q: Asha says 3 × 102 = 3 × 100 + 2 = 302. What is wrong?
qa.a: She must add 3 × 2 = 6, so it is 306

qa.q: A cow gives 12 litres of milk a day. How much milk does it give in 7 days?
qa.e: 7 equal groups of 12: 12 × 7 = 84 litres.

qa.q: A farm has 24 cows. Each gives 15 litres a day. How many litres in all?
Milk costs ₹56 a litre. What do 5 litres cost?
A dairy packs 36 paneer cubes in a tray. How many cubes are in 25 trays?
Meena puts 4 rows of 6 milk bottles in a crate. How many bottles are in the crate?
qa.e: 4 rows of 6 is 4 × 6 = 24 bottles.

qa.q: Kabir's cows gave 145 litres on Monday. On Tuesday they gave double that. How much on Tuesday?
qa.e: Double means × 2: 145 × 2 = 290 L.

qa.q: Which of these is the same as 23 × 14?
qa.e: Split 14 into 10 and 4. Multiply 23 by each part and add: 23 × 10 + 23 × 4.

qa.q: A milk van carries 18 cans. Each can holds 40 litres. How many litres does the van carry?
What is 23 × 14?
In the grid method for 34 × 26, which four parts are added?
What is 34 × 26?
Nida does 45 × 12 as 45 × 10 + 45 × 2. John does 12 × 45 as 12 × 40 + 12 × 5. Who is right?
qa.e: Both split a factor correctly. 450 + 90 = 540 and 480 + 60 = 540.

qa.q: A theatre has 24 rows of 35 seats. How many seats?
A batter scores 48 runs in each of 12 matches. How many runs in all?
A shop bill: 18 kg of rice at ₹45 a kg. What is the bill?
A library has 36 shelves with 28 books on each. How many books?
What is 234 × 6?
What is 312 × 24?
In long multiplication of 312 × 24, why do we put a 0 at the start of the second row?
qa.a: Because we are multiplying by 2 tens, which is 20
qa.e: The 2 in 24 stands for 20, so the row shows 312 × 20.

qa.q: A dairy sells 312 litres a day. How much in 24 days?
What is 123 × 111?
What is 205 × 104?
A school buys 145 notebooks at ₹32 each. What is the cost?
A truck carries 250 sacks, each 48 kg. How many kg in all?
Sonu wrote 46 × 23 = 138 + 92 = 230. What is the correct answer?
What mistake did Sonu make in 46 × 23?
qa.e: The 2 in 23 is 2 tens, so 46 × 2 tens = 920.

qa.q: Pinky wrote 312 × 200 = 6,240. What is right?
qa.e: 312 × 2 = 624, and × 100 adds two zeros: 62,400.

qa.q: Raj wrote 58 × 7 = 356. What is correct?
qa.e: 8 × 7 = 56: write 6, carry 5. 5 × 7 = 35, plus 5 = 40. Answer 406.

qa.q: Which is a quick way to see that 46 × 23 = 230 is wrong?
qa.e: An estimate shows the answer should be near 1,000, not 230.

qa.q: Meera wrote 25 × 70 = 175. What is the correct product?
qa.e: 25 × 7 = 175, then × 10 = 1,750. She treated 70 as 7.

qa.q: Kabir did 134 × 21 as 134 + 268 = 402. What is the correct answer?
Which working for 27 × 15 is correct?
Which product has the same answer as 12 × 15, without working it out?
qa.e: Halve 12 and double 15: 6 × 30. Both are 180.

qa.q: What is 199 × 63?
Which is the easiest way to find 16 × 25?
Red × Red = 64 and Red × Blue = 40. What is Blue?
qa.e: Red = 8 because 8 × 8 = 64. 8 × Blue = 40, so Blue = 5.

qa.q: Green × 9 = 63 and Green + Yellow = 10. What is Yellow?
qa.e: Green = 7 since 7 × 9 = 63. 7 + Yellow = 10, so Yellow = 3.

qa.q: Blue × Blue = 36 and Blue × Pink = 54. What is Pink?
qa.e: Blue = 6, and 6 × 9 = 54, so Pink = 9.

qa.q: Estimate 48 × 21. Which is closest?
Estimate 62 × 39. Which is closest?
Which product is about 600?
Kavi says 52 × 49 = 548. Use an estimate to judge.
qa.e: 50 × 50 = 2,500, so 548 is far too small. (The exact answer is 2,548.)

qa.q: 9 school bags cost ₹98 each. About how much do they cost?
A reward starts at ₹1 on day 1 and doubles each day. How much is given on day 6?
Starting with ₹1 and tripling each day, how much on day 5?
Starting with ₹1 and multiplying by 5 each day, how much on day 4?
Which reward is bigger on day 10: ₹1 doubled every day, or a fixed ₹100 each day?
qa.e: Doubling gives ₹512 on day 10, more than ₹100.

qa.q: Total of ₹1 doubling for 5 days (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 16) is how much?

qa.e: 48 is double 24, so the product doubles: 720.
18 is half of 36, so the product is halved: 360.

qa.q: In the row 3, 8, 2, 9, 5, which two neighbours have the largest product?
In the row 3, 8, 2, 9, 5, which two neighbours have the smallest product?
A farmer gets 48 litres of milk in the morning and 36 litres in the evening. He fills 2-litre bottles. How many bottles?
qa.e: Total milk: 48 + 36 = 84 L. Bottles: 84 ÷ 2 = 42.

qa.q: Aisha buys 4 packets of paneer at ₹85 each. She pays ₹500. How much change does she get?
A dairy sends 360 litres of milk each day, shared equally among 9 shops. How much does one shop get in 7 days?
qa.e: One shop gets 360 ÷ 9 = 40 L a day. In 7 days: 40 × 7 = 280 L.

qa.q: There are 6 crates with 24 bottles in each. Which operation finds the total number of bottles?
qa.e: 6 equal groups of 24 means multiply: 6 × 24 = 144.

qa.q: Harpreet has ₹250. A box of ghee costs ₹65. How many boxes can she buy?
qa.e: 65 × 3 = 195 and 65 × 4 = 260, which is more than ₹250. So she can buy 3 boxes.

qa.q: A cow eats 8 kg of fodder a day. How much do 5 cows eat in 10 days?
qa.e: One day for 5 cows: 8 × 5 = 40 kg. For 10 days: 40 × 10 = 400 kg.

qa.q: 12 children share 3 boxes of 20 laddoos equally. How many laddoos does each child get?
qa.e: Total laddoos: 3 × 20 = 60. Each child: 60 ÷ 12 = 5.

qa.q: Kabir says: '126 ÷ 6 = 21. I can check it by working out 21 × 6.' Is he right?
qa.a: Yes, multiplying back checks a division
qa.e: 21 × 6 = 126, which gives back the starting number. Multiplying undoes dividing.

qa.q: A dairy has 144 litres of milk. It fills 6 cans equally. How much milk goes in each can?
96 eggs are packed in trays of 12. How many trays are needed?
50 laddoos are shared equally among 8 friends. How many does each get, and how many are left?
qa.e: 8 × 6 = 48. 50 − 48 = 2 left. Each gets 6.

qa.q: Riya's family earns ₹1,800 for milk over 30 days, the same each day. How much is that per day?
130 children go on a dairy trip. Each bus seats 40. How many buses are needed so no one is left behind?
qa.e: 130 ÷ 40 = 3 remainder 10. The 10 extra children need one more bus, so 4 buses.

qa.q: 7 × ? = 84. What is the missing number?
What is 225 ÷ 5?
Aisha shares 18 cups of curd equally into 3 baskets. How many cups go in each basket?
qa.e: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cups in each basket.

qa.q: A strip goes over 1, under 1. If it starts with over, what does it do at the 6th crossing?
qa.e: Odd crossings are over and even crossings are under. 6 is even, so under.

qa.q: Row rule: over 2, under 1. What is the 7th crossing if the row starts with over?
qa.e: The core O O U has 3 crossings. 7 = 3 + 3 + 1, so the 7th is like the 1st: over.

qa.q: What is the rule for this row? O O U O O U O O U
qa.e: Two overs then one under repeat.

qa.q: With 'over 1, under 1' and a shift of one each row, which row looks exactly like row 1?
qa.e: Row 2 is shifted, row 3 is shifted back, matching row 1.

qa.q: With 'over 2, under 1' and a shift of one each row, after how many rows does the pattern repeat?
qa.e: The core is 3 long, so after 3 shifts it lines up again: row 4 = row 1.

qa.q: Row 1 is O U U O U U. Row 2 starts one place later. What does row 2 start with?
qa.e: Shifting one place, row 2 starts with what row 1 has at the end: U, giving U O U U O U.

qa.q: A pattern on grid paper has rows: ■□■□, □■□■, ■□■□, ___. What comes in row 4?
qa.e: Rows take turns: rows 1 and 3 are the same, so row 4 is like row 2.

qa.q: Which tool helps you check a weaving pattern before you weave?
qa.a: Drawing it row by row on grid paper
qa.e: Grid paper lets you draw each row with its rule and shift.

qa.q: What comes next? ▲ ● ▲ ● ▲ ?
qa.e: The core is ▲ ●. After ▲ comes ●.

qa.q: What is the core of this pattern? 🔴 🔵 🔵 🔴 🔵 🔵 🔴 🔵 🔵
qa.e: 🔴 🔵 🔵 is the part that repeats.

qa.q: In ■ ▲ ● ■ ▲ ● …, what is the 12th shape?
qa.e: The core has 3 shapes. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 full cores, so the 12th shape is the last in the core: ●.

qa.q: The pattern ⭐ 🌙 🌙 repeats. How many stars are in the first 15 shapes?
qa.e: 15 shapes make 15 ÷ 3 = 5 cores. Each core has 1 star, so 5 stars.

qa.q: Riya's rangoli border goes red, yellow, green, red, yellow, green, … What colour is the 20th tile?
qa.e: The core has 3 colours. 20 = 3 × 6 + 2, so the 20th is the 2nd colour: yellow.

qa.q: Each arrow is the one before turned a quarter turn clockwise: ↑ → ↓ ? What comes next?
qa.e: A quarter turn clockwise from ↓ (down) points ← (left).

qa.q: Kabir strings beads: 2 red, 1 white, 2 red, 1 white, … He uses 18 beads. How many are red?
qa.e: Each core has 3 beads, 2 of them red. 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cores. 6 × 2 = 12 red.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT a repeating pattern?
qa.e: 3 5 8 2 9 1 has no part that repeats.

qa.q: What comes next? 3, 6, 9, 12, ?
qa.e: The rule is add 3. 12 + 3 = 15.

qa.q: Matchstick squares in a row use 4, 7, 10, … sticks. How many sticks for 6 squares?
qa.e: Start with 4 and add 3 for each extra square: 4 + 3 × 5 = 19.

qa.q: Dots make triangles: 1, 3, 6, 10, … What comes next?
qa.e: It adds 2, then 3, then 4, so next add 5: 10 + 5 = 15.

qa.q: Arjun builds towers of 2, 4, 8, 16 blocks. Each tower doubles. How many blocks in the next tower?
Square dot patterns have 1, 4, 9, 16 dots. How many dots in the next square?
qa.e: The squares are 1×1, 2×2, 3×3, 4×4. Next is 5×5 = 25.

qa.q: Matchstick triangles in a row: 1 triangle uses 3 sticks, 2 use 5, 3 use 7. How many sticks for 10 triangles?
qa.e: Each new triangle adds 2 sticks. 3 + 2 × 9 = 21.

qa.q: What is the rule? 5, 9, 13, 17, …
qa.e: Each number is 4 more than the one before.

qa.q: Meena counts down: 100, 90, 80, 70, … What is the 8th number?
qa.e: Each step takes away 10. The 8th number is 7 steps after 100: 100 − 70 = 30.

qa.q: Which shape cannot tile a floor on its own without gaps?
qa.e: Circles have curved edges, so gaps are always left between them.

qa.q: In a floor of square tiles, how many squares meet at one corner point?
qa.e: Each square corner is 90°. 360° ÷ 90° = 4.

qa.q: Honeybees build their honeycomb with cells of which shape?
qa.e: Honeycomb cells are hexagons. They fit together with no gaps.

qa.q: How many regular hexagons meet at one point in a hexagon tiling?
qa.e: Each hexagon corner is 120°. 360° ÷ 120° = 3.

qa.q: A floor is 5 tiles long and 4 tiles wide. How many tiles cover it?
qa.e: 4 rows of 5 tiles: 5 × 4 = 20.

qa.q: In tiling, what does 'no overlaps' mean?
qa.a: Tiles do not sit on top of each other
qa.e: Overlap means one tile covers part of another. A tiling has none.

qa.q: How many equilateral triangles meet at one point in a triangle tiling?
qa.e: Each corner of an equilateral triangle is 60°. 360° ÷ 60° = 6.

qa.q: Aisha's bathroom wall needs 6 rows of 8 tiles. She has 40 tiles. How many more does she need?
qa.e: She needs 6 × 8 = 48 tiles. 48 − 40 = 8 more.

qa.q: Why can't 5 squares meet at one point on a flat floor?
qa.a: Their corners add to 450°, more than a full turn
qa.e: 5 × 90° = 450°, which is more than 360°, so they overlap.

qa.q: What angle is left when 2 regular octagons (135° each) meet at a point?
Which shape fills the gap between 2 regular octagons at a point?
qa.e: The gap is 90°, exactly one square corner.

qa.q: How many equilateral triangles fit with 2 squares around a point?
qa.e: 2 squares take 180°. 360° − 180° = 180°. Each triangle is 60°, so 3 triangles.

qa.q: A tiling has 1 hexagon and some triangles at each corner. How many triangles?
Do regular octagons tile a floor on their own?
qa.e: 2 octagons leave a 90° gap and 3 would need 405°. So they cannot tile alone.

qa.q: At each corner of a tiling you see: square, triangle, square, triangle, triangle. Is it a full turn?
qa.e: Two squares (180°) and three triangles (180°) make 360°.

qa.q: Rina cuts out squares and equilateral triangles of the same side. Which set around a point works?
qa.e: 2 × 90° + 3 × 60° = 360°. 3 squares + 2 triangles = 390°, too much.

qa.q: A triangle has sides 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm. What kind of triangle is it?
qa.e: All three sides are equal, so it is equilateral.

qa.q: A triangle has sides 4 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm. What kind is it?
qa.e: No two sides are equal, so it is scalene.

qa.q: Which triangle has exactly two equal sides?
qa.e: 5, 5 and 8 has exactly two equal sides: isosceles.

qa.q: A set square has one square corner. What kind of triangle is it?
qa.e: A triangle with a right angle is a right-angled triangle.

qa.q: An equilateral triangle has one angle of 60°. What are the other two angles?
qa.e: In an equilateral triangle all angles are equal.

qa.q: Two matching right-angled triangles are joined along their longest sides. Which shape can they make?
qa.e: The two right angles end up at opposite corners and the shape has 4 square corners: a rectangle.

qa.q: Two matching equilateral triangles are joined along a side. How many sides does the new shape have?
qa.e: Each triangle has 3 sides. The joined side is hidden: 3 + 3 − 2 = 4 sides.

qa.q: Can a triangle be both right-angled and isosceles?
qa.a: Yes, with two equal sides around the square corner
qa.e: Half of a square cut along its diagonal has a right angle and two equal sides.

qa.q: A shape has opposite sides equal and parallel, but no right angles. What is it?
qa.e: Opposite sides equal and parallel is a parallelogram. Without right angles it is not a rectangle.

qa.q: Which shape has two pairs of equal sides next to each other?
qa.e: That is the rule for a kite.

qa.q: Which is true?
qa.e: A square has all a rectangle needs: 4 right angles and opposite sides equal.

qa.q: A rectangle has all sides equal. What is its special name?
qa.e: A rectangle with all sides equal is a square.

qa.q: Sides are 6 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm, 4 cm going round, with 4 right angles. What is it?
qa.e: Opposite sides equal with all right angles: rectangle. Not all sides are equal, so not a square.

qa.q: Sides going round are 3 cm, 3 cm, 7 cm, 7 cm. What is it?
qa.e: The equal sides are next to each other in pairs: a kite.

qa.q: Which shape is always a parallelogram?
qa.e: A rectangle has opposite sides equal and parallel.

qa.q: How is a square different from other rectangles?
qa.e: All rectangles have right angles and opposite sides equal; only a square has all sides equal.

qa.q: A quadrilateral measures 7 cm, 4 cm, 7 cm, 4 cm going round. Which family does it belong to?
qa.e: Opposite sides are equal, so it is in the parallelogram family.

qa.q: A quadrilateral measures 5 cm, 5 cm, 9 cm, 9 cm going round. What is it?
qa.e: Equal sides are next to each other, so it is a kite.

qa.q: On grid paper a shape has corners at (0,0), (4,0), (5,2) and (1,2). What is it?
qa.e: The top side is the bottom side slid across: both 4 long and parallel. That makes a parallelogram.

qa.q: How do you draw a kite on grid paper?
qa.a: Draw a line of symmetry and put matching sides on both sides of it
qa.e: A kite is symmetric about one diagonal, so the sides on each side match.

qa.q: A rhombus is cut along one diagonal. What pieces do you get?
qa.e: A diagonal joins two opposite corners and splits the shape into 2 triangles.

qa.q: One corner is cut off a rhombus with a straight cut. How many sides does the bigger piece have?
qa.e: One corner is replaced by a new short side with two corners, so 4 + 1 = 5 sides.

qa.q: Sides 6, 6, 6, 6 cm with no right angles. What is it?
qa.e: All sides equal without right angles is a rhombus.

qa.q: The two triangles from a rhombus cut along a diagonal are rejoined so the cut sides do not touch. Which shape can they make?
qa.e: Matching triangles joined along another pair of equal sides make a parallelogram.

qa.q: How many pieces are there in a tangram?
qa.e: 2 large + 1 medium + 2 small triangles + 1 square + 1 parallelogram = 7.

qa.q: How many triangles are in a tangram set?
qa.e: 2 large + 1 medium + 2 small = 5 triangles.

qa.q: Which tangram piece has 4 right angles?
qa.e: Only the square has four square corners.

qa.q: Which two pieces together can make the tangram square?
qa.e: Two small triangles join along their long sides to make the square.

qa.q: How are all the tangram triangles alike?
qa.a: Each has a right angle and two equal sides
qa.e: They are all right-angled isosceles triangles, in different sizes.

qa.q: Clue: 'I have 4 equal sides.' Which shapes fit?
qa.e: Both a square and a rhombus have 4 equal sides.

qa.q: Clues: 'I have 3 sides. All my sides are equal.' Which shape am I?
qa.e: 3 equal sides means an equilateral triangle.

qa.q: Clues: '4 sides. Opposite sides are equal. 4 right angles. Sides not all equal.' Which shape am I?
qa.e: Opposite sides equal and right angles: rectangle. Sides not all equal: not a square.

qa.q: Which shape do you get when you join the four ends of two diameters of a circle?
qa.e: The two diameters are equal and cut each other in half, which makes a rectangle.

qa.q: When does joining the ends of two diameters give a square?
qa.a: When the diameters cross at right angles
qa.e: Diameters crossing at right angles make all four sides equal: a square.

qa.q: How many matching triangles does the fold line split a paper kite into?
qa.e: The kite's line of symmetry splits it into 2 matching triangles.

qa.q: A paper kite is made by folding a square. What kind of shape is a kite?
qa.a: A quadrilateral with two pairs of equal neighbouring sides
qa.e: A kite has 4 sides with neighbouring sides equal in pairs.

qa.q: A rangoli design has 8 equally spaced points on a circle joined to the centre. How many equal angles are made at the centre?
qa.e: 8 lines from the centre make 8 equal parts of the full turn.

qa.q: Each of those 8 equal angles at the centre is how many degrees?
To draw a square inside a circle with all four corners on the circle, what do you draw first?
qa.e: Their four ends are the corners of the square.

qa.q: Points A and C are ends of one diameter; B and D are ends of another. What is true about AC and BD?
qa.e: All diameters of one circle are the same length.

qa.q: How many squares does a net of a cube have?
qa.e: A cube has 6 faces, so its net has 6 squares.

qa.q: A cube net has squares in a row: 1, 2, 3, 4, with 5 above square 2 and 6 below square 2. Which face is opposite 1?
qa.e: In a row of four, the 1st and 3rd squares end up opposite each other.

qa.q: In the same net (row 1, 2, 3, 4; 5 above 2; 6 below 2), which face is opposite 5?
qa.e: 5 and 6 both join square 2, one above and one below, so they fold to opposite faces.

qa.q: A 3×3×3 cube frame keeps only the cubes along the edges. How many small cubes are removed?
qa.e: Frame = 8 corners + 12 edge cubes = 20. 27 − 20 = 7 removed.

qa.q: How many small cubes are removed to make a 5×5×5 cube frame?
A 3×3×3 cube is painted on all sides. How many small cubes have exactly 2 painted faces?
qa.e: The middle cube of each of the 12 edges has 2 painted faces.

qa.q: In that painted 3×3×3 cube, how many small cubes have no paint at all?
qa.e: Only the very centre cube is hidden from every side.

qa.q: In that painted cube, how many small cubes have exactly 1 painted face?
qa.e: The centre cube of each of the 6 faces has 1 painted face.

qa.q: Clues: The triangle is left of the circle. The square is right of the circle. The star is left of the triangle. What is the order from the left?
qa.e: Star is before triangle, triangle before circle, circle before square.

qa.q: What shape are the faces of an icosahedron?
qa.e: All 20 faces of an icosahedron are equilateral triangles.

qa.q: What shape are the faces of a dodecahedron?
qa.e: A dodecahedron has 12 regular pentagon faces.

qa.q: An icosahedron has 20 triangle faces. Each edge is shared by 2 faces. How many edges?
qa.e: 20 × 3 = 60 sides, but each edge is counted twice: 60 ÷ 2 = 30.

qa.q: A dodecahedron has 12 pentagon faces. How many edges does it have?
qa.e: 12 × 5 = 60 sides, shared by 2 faces each: 60 ÷ 2 = 30.

qa.q: How many faces meet at each corner of an icosahedron?
qa.e: 5 equilateral triangles meet at every corner of an icosahedron.

qa.q: Which is NOT a Platonic solid?
qa.e: A cylinder has curved surfaces, not identical regular polygon faces.

qa.q: How many straws are needed to build a tetrahedron (4 triangle faces)?
qa.e: A tetrahedron has 6 edges, so 6 straws: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6.

qa.q: Which weight makes sense for a mango?
qa.e: A mango is light but not tiny: about 250 g.

qa.q: Which is a silly weight claim?
qa.e: A pencil weighs only a few grams.

qa.q: A scale between 0 and 1 kg has 10 equal marks. What does each mark show?
qa.e: 1,000 g ÷ 10 marks = 100 g per mark.

qa.q: On that scale, the pointer is 6 marks past 2 kg. What is the weight in grams?
A scale has 4 equal marks between 0 and 1 kg. What does each mark show?
On a double number line, which gram value lines up with 3 kg?
What sits halfway between 1 kg and 2 kg on a double number line?
qa.e: Halfway between 1,000 g and 2,000 g is 1,500 g.

qa.q: Which is the most sensible weight for a 10-year-old child?
qa.e: Children of this age weigh around 25–35 kg.

qa.q: Which unit should we use to weigh a watermelon?
qa.e: A watermelon is heavy, so kilograms fit best.

qa.q: Which unit should we use to weigh a 1-rupee coin?
qa.e: A coin is very light, so grams fit best.

qa.q: On a balance, Riya puts a mango on one side and a lemon on the other. The mango side goes down. What does this tell us?
qa.e: The heavier side always goes down.

qa.q: How many grams make 1 kilogram?
qa.e: Kilo means thousand. 1 kg = 1,000 g.

qa.q: Which is the heaviest?
qa.e: 1 kg 50 g = 1,050 g. That is more than 1,005 g and 900 g.

qa.q: 4 packets of dal weigh 250 g each. What is their total weight?
Kabir weighs 32 kg. His little sister weighs 19 kg. How much heavier is Kabir?
A bag holds 5 kg of rice. Meena uses 750 g. How many grams are left?
Which sign goes in: 1 kg 50 g ☐ 1,500 g?
qa.e: 1 kg 50 g = 1,050 g, and 1,050 g is less than 1,500 g.

qa.q: Which list goes from heaviest to lightest?
3 kg 450 g = ? g
Write 7,500 ml in litres and millilitres.
For Diwali, Aisha bought 1 kg 250 g of kaju katli and 750 g of laddoos. What is the total weight?
A 1 L bottle has 350 ml of water in it. How much more water will fill it?
Which is heavier: 2,500 g or 2 kg 50 g?
qa.e: 2 kg 50 g = 2,050 g, which is less than 2,500 g.

qa.q: A shop has 10 kg of sugar. It packs it into 500 g packets. How many packets?
A cook uses 3 L 200 ml of milk for kheer and 1 L 900 ml for chai. How much milk in millilitres?
How many grams are in a quarter of a kilogram?
qa.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. A quarter is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g.

qa.q: How many milligrams make 1 gram?
qa.e: 1 g = 1,000 mg, just like 1 kg = 1,000 g.

qa.q: Write 3 g in milligrams.
Write 4 g 100 mg in milligrams.
Write 4 g 50 mg in milligrams.
qa.e: 4,000 + 50 = 4,050 mg. The 50 sits in the tens and ones places.

qa.q: Write 2,350 mg in g and mg.
qa.e: 2,000 mg = 2 g, and 350 mg is left.

qa.q: A tablet has 500 mg of medicine. How many tablets make 1 g?
Which is heavier: 1 g 80 mg or 1,800 mg?
qa.e: 1 g 80 mg = 1,080 mg, which is less than 1,800 mg.

qa.q: Which unit is best for weighing a grain of rice?
qa.e: A grain of rice is very light, so mg is best.

qa.q: How many kilograms make 1 quintal?
qa.e: 1 quintal = 100 kg.

qa.q: How many kilograms make 1 tonne?
qa.e: 1 tonne = 1,000 kg.

qa.q: A truck carries 12 tonnes of sand. How many kg is that?
A farmer has 850 kg of rice. How many full quintals is that, and how many kg are left?
How many quintals make 1 tonne?
qa.e: 1 tonne = 1,000 kg and 1 quintal = 100 kg. 1,000 ÷ 100 = 10.

qa.q: Which unit is best to weigh a loaded goods train?
qa.e: A goods train is enormously heavy, so tonnes are best.

qa.q: An elephant weighs about 5,000 kg and a cow about 500 kg. About how many times heavier is the elephant?
A rhino weighs about 2 tonnes. A hippo weighs about 3 times as much as a 500 kg buffalo. Which is heavier?
qa.e: Rhino = 2,000 kg. Hippo = 3 × 500 = 1,500 kg. The rhino is heavier.

qa.q: A king weighs 10 times as much as a 9 kg sack. What does he weigh?
The king weighed 90 kg. A year later he weighed 98 kg. How much weight did he gain?
A prince weighs 10 times as much as a 4 kg pumpkin. Later he gains 5 kg. What does he weigh now?
Onions cost ₹40 a kg. What do 3 kg cost?
Grapes cost ₹80 a kg. What does 1/2 kg cost?
qa.e: Half a kg costs half the price: ₹80 ÷ 2 = ₹40.

qa.q: Paneer costs ₹360 a kg. What does 250 g cost?
Apples cost ₹120 a kg. What do 1 kg 500 g cost?
Tomatoes cost ₹48 a kg. What do 2 kg 250 g cost?
500 g of rice feeds 4 people. How much rice for 8 people?
qa.e: 8 is double 4, so double 500 g = 1,000 g = 1 kg.

qa.q: 600 g of flour makes rotis for 6 people. How much for 3 people?
qa.e: 3 is half of 6, so half of 600 g = 300 g.

qa.q: A scrap dealer pays ₹60 for 5 kg of newspaper. How much for 1 kg?
At ₹12 per kg, how much for 8 kg of newspaper?
3 kg of iron scrap fetch ₹75. How much do 7 kg fetch?
A recipe uses 250 g of sugar for 5 people. How much for 15 people?
qa.e: 15 is 3 times 5, so 3 × 250 g = 750 g.

qa.q: On a double number line, 4 kg ↔ ₹100. What lines up with 6 kg?
A kabadiwala pays ₹8 a kg for plastic. Sonu gets ₹56. How many kg did he sell?
Which unit should we use for a spoonful of cough syrup?
qa.e: A spoonful is a small amount, so millilitres fit best.

qa.q: Which of these holds about 1 litre?
qa.e: A common water bottle holds about 1 L.

qa.q: A glass holds 250 ml. How many glasses fill a 1 L jug?
Arjun drinks 6 glasses of water. Each glass holds 200 ml. How much does he drink?
qa.e: 6 × 200 = 1,200 ml, which is 1 L 200 ml.

qa.q: Jug A holds 750 ml. Jug B holds 1 L. Which jug holds more?
qa.e: 1 L = 1,000 ml, which is more than 750 ml.

qa.q: A bucket holds 15 L. A mug holds 500 ml. How many mugs fill the bucket?
A water tank had 50 L. The family used 18 L. How much is left?
A 2 L bottle of mango juice is poured into cups of 200 ml. How many cups are filled?
A jug is marked in ml. At which mark is 1 litre?
At which ml mark is 2 L 500 ml?
A vessel is filled to the 3,000 ml line. How many litres is that?
Meena drinks 1 L 600 ml on Monday and 1 L 800 ml on Tuesday. How much in all?
A cow gives 4 L 500 ml in the morning and 3 L 750 ml in the evening. How much in a day?
A plant gets 750 ml of water every day. How much in 4 days?
qa.e: 4 × 750 = 3,000 ml, which is 3 L.

qa.q: Over three days a family uses 12 L 300 ml, 11 L 500 ml and 10 L 400 ml of milk. Total in ml?
A bottle marked in ml is filled to 1,250 ml. Is that more or less than 1 L?
A petrol pump sold 1,250 L on Monday and 980 L on Tuesday. How much on both days?
How much more was sold on Monday (1,250 L) than Tuesday (980 L)?
Record: Wed 1,075 L, Thu 1,320 L, Fri 1,500 L. On which day was the most sold?
qa.e: 1,500 L is the largest.

qa.q: Using Wed 1,075 L, Thu 1,320 L, Fri 1,500 L, what is the total for the three days?
Which sign goes in: 2 L 50 ml ☐ 2,500 ml?
qa.e: 2 L 50 ml = 2,050 ml, which is less than 2,500 ml.

qa.q: Which sign goes in: 1,500 ml ☐ 1 L 500 ml?
qa.e: 1 L 500 ml = 1,500 ml. They are equal.

qa.q: Which holds the most?
qa.e: In ml: 5 L 20 ml = 5,020 ml, then 5,002 ml, 5 L 200 ml = 5,200 ml and 5,120 ml. 5 L 200 ml is the most.

qa.q: Diesel sold on Saturday was 1,180 L, and on Sunday 245 L less. How much on Sunday?
8 containers each hold 1 L 75 ml. How much do they hold in all?
6 bottles each hold 750 ml. What is the total in ml?
9 L of lassi is shared equally into 6 jugs. How much in each jug?
A 20 L can of oil is poured into 4 equal tins. How much in each tin?
Milk costs ₹56 a litre. What do 4 L cost?
Milk costs ₹60 a litre. What do 2 L 500 ml cost?
qa.e: 2 L cost ₹120 and 500 ml (half a litre) costs ₹30. Total ₹150.

qa.q: A juice stall sells 120 glasses at ₹15 each. How much does it earn?
How many 250 ml glasses can be filled from 30 L of juice?
18 coconuts are put in rows of 6. How many rows are there?
20 coconuts are packed in bags of 3. How many full bags are there, and how many are left over?
qa.e: 3 × 6 = 18, so 6 full bags. 20 − 18 = 2 left.

qa.q: Which way can 15 coconuts be put in equal rows with none left over?
qa.e: 3 × 5 = 15 exactly.

qa.q: Riya puts 36 coconuts into 4 equal heaps. How many coconuts are in each heap?
qa.e: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 coconuts in each heap.

qa.q: In how many different ways can 12 coconuts be put in equal rows? (2 rows of 6 and 6 rows of 2 count as the same.)
A farmer packs 45 coconuts into boxes. Each box holds 10. How many boxes does he need to pack all of them?
qa.e: 4 boxes hold 40. The last 5 coconuts need one more box, so 5 boxes.

qa.q: Which number of coconuts can NOT be put in 2 or more equal rows with 2 or more in each row?
qa.e: 7 can only be 1 row of 7. 8 = 2 × 4, 9 = 3 × 3 and 10 = 2 × 5.

qa.q: Kabir puts 5 coconuts in each of 8 baskets. He has 3 coconuts left over. How many coconuts did he have?
What is 73 ÷ 1?
qa.e: Dividing by 1 makes one group with everything in it, so the answer is the number itself.

qa.q: An array has 4 rows of 7 coconuts. Which division fact does it show?
qa.e: 4 × 7 = 28, so 28 coconuts in 4 rows gives 7 in each row.

qa.q: Which is NOT in the fact family of 8 × 9 = 72?
qa.e: 72 ÷ 2 = 36 is true, but it uses 2 and 36, not 8 and 9.

qa.q: Division is the opposite of which operation?
qa.e: Division undoes multiplication: 5 × 6 = 30 and 30 ÷ 6 = 5.

qa.q: ? × 7 = 63. What is the missing number?
96 ÷ ? = 8. What is the missing number?
48 ÷ 2 = 24, 48 ÷ 4 = 12, 48 ÷ 8 = ? What comes next in the pattern?
qa.e: The divisor doubles each time, so the answer halves: 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

qa.q: Which pair of division statements comes from 6 × 15 = 90?
qa.e: Divide the product by each factor to get the other factor.
Each digit moves two places right: 3,700 → 37.

qa.q: What is 860 ÷ 10?
qa.e: Each digit moves one place right: 860 → 86.
360 is 10 times 36, and the divisor is the same, so the answer is 10 times 9.
7,200 is 100 times 72, so the quotient is 100 times 9 = 900.

qa.q: How many ₹100 notes make ₹6,500?
A family drives 540 km in 6 days, the same distance each day. How far each day?
₹2,800 is shared equally among 7 friends. How much does each get?
The same digit goes in every box: ☐ × 4 = 20, 20 ÷ ☐ = 4, ☐ + 15 = 20, 25 − ☐ = 20. What is it?
What is 96 ÷ 4?
Which is a good way to break 84 for 84 ÷ 7?
qa.e: Both 70 and 14 are in the 7 times table.

qa.q: What is 156 ÷ 6?
What is 135 ÷ 5?
Ravi did 75 ÷ 3 as 60 ÷ 3 + 15 ÷ 3. What answer does he get?
Which is NOT a correct way to work out 48 ÷ 4?
qa.e: Every part must be divided by the same number, 4.

qa.q: 208 children sit in 8 equal rows. How many in each row?
How can you check that 96 ÷ 4 = 24?
qa.a: Multiply 24 × 4 and see if you get 96
qa.e: Multiplication undoes division, so 24 × 4 should be 96.

qa.q: In 95 ÷ 6 = 15 remainder 5, which number is the divisor?
qa.e: The divisor is the number we divide by.

qa.q: In 95 ÷ 6 = 15 remainder 5, which number is the quotient?
qa.e: The quotient is the answer of the division.

qa.q: What is 87 ÷ 4?
Which remainder is impossible when dividing by 5?
qa.e: A remainder must be less than the divisor 5, so 6 is impossible.

qa.q: Check: a division has divisor 7, quotient 12 and remainder 4. What is the dividend?
Sita wrote 50 ÷ 7 = 6 remainder 8. What is correct?
qa.e: The remainder 8 is more than 7, so one more 7 fits: 7 × 7 = 49, and 50 − 49 = 1.

qa.q: In long division of 156 ÷ 6, what is the first step?
qa.e: 1 hundred is less than 6, so we look at 15 tens. 6 × 2 = 12 tens, leaving 3 tens.

qa.q: Use long division: what is the quotient of 156 ÷ 6?
qa.e: 15 tens ÷ 6 = 2 tens r 3 tens. Bring down 6: 36 ÷ 6 = 6. Answer 26.

qa.q: What is 675 ÷ 5?
qa.e: 6 hundreds ÷ 5 = 1 r 1; 17 tens ÷ 5 = 3 r 2; 25 ÷ 5 = 5. Answer 135.

qa.q: What is 336 ÷ 12?
What is 945 ÷ 15?
What is 538 ÷ 4?
Five friends share a ₹675 bill equally. How much does each pay?
Four cousins share a ₹1,000 gift equally. How much does each get?
Which uses only ₹50 and ₹20 notes to make ₹170?
qa.e: 150 + 20 = 170. The others make 140, 150 and 190.

qa.q: How many ₹20 notes make ₹260?
8 coconuts give 1 litre of oil. How many litres do 320 coconuts give?
qa.e: 320 ÷ 8 = 40 litres.

qa.q: The mill sells 40 litres at ₹250 a litre. How much does it earn?
Coir sells at ₹30 a kg. The mill earned ₹1,800 from coir. How many kg were sold?
Making 1 litre of oil costs ₹180. It sells for ₹250. What is the profit on 1 litre?
Using that profit of ₹70 a litre, what is the profit on 25 litres?
A farmer sells 600 coconuts at ₹15 each. He spent ₹4,500 growing them. What is his profit?
Oil is sold in 500 ml bottles at ₹130 each. The mill earns ₹3,900. How many bottles were sold?
Which tells us whether a business made a profit?
qa.a: Selling price is more than cost price
qa.e: Profit happens when we sell for more than it cost.

qa.q: What is 4,536 ÷ 6?
In 2,835 ÷ 5, why do we start with 28 hundreds?
qa.a: Because 2 thousands is less than 5, so we regroup them as 20 hundreds
qa.e: 2 thousands cannot be shared among 5, so we change them to 20 hundreds and add the 8 hundreds.

qa.q: What is 2,835 ÷ 5?
What is 3,612 ÷ 3?
A farm packs 9,750 coconuts into bags of 25. How many bags?
I am a 3-digit number less than 200. I can be divided exactly by 5 and by 9. My digits add to 9. I am even. Who am I?
qa.e: Divisible by 5 and 9 means a multiple of 45: 135, 180 (3-digit, under 200). Both have digit sum 9. Even: 180.

qa.q: A 3-digit number is 4 × 125 and ends in 0. What is it?
A hall seats 250. 1,800 people want to see a show. How many shows are needed?
qa.e: 1,800 ÷ 250 = 7 r 50. The 50 people need one more show: 8 shows.

qa.q: The puppet group can do 3 shows a day. How many days for 8 shows?
qa.e: 8 ÷ 3 = 2 r 2. Two shows are left for a third day.

qa.q: ₹840 is shared equally among 4 children to spend over 7 days. How much can each child spend a day?
qa.e: Each child gets ₹840 ÷ 4 = ₹210. Per day: ₹210 ÷ 7 = ₹30.

qa.q: 120 bananas are shared by 5 monkeys over 3 days, equally. How many does each monkey eat a day?
qa.e: Each monkey gets 120 ÷ 5 = 24. Per day 24 ÷ 3 = 8.
Both numbers are 10 times bigger, so the quotient stays 4.

qa.q: Which division has the same answer as 56 ÷ 7?
qa.e: Multiplying both numbers by 10 keeps the quotient: 8.

qa.q: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 and 36 ÷ 2 = 18. What happens to the quotient when the divisor is halved?
qa.e: Smaller groups mean more groups: 9 → 18.

qa.q: A bus seats 45. How many trips to carry 200 pilgrims?
qa.e: 200 ÷ 45 = 4 r 20. The last 20 need one more trip: 5.

qa.q: 'Raju bought some pens for ₹60. How much did one pen cost?' What is missing?
qa.e: To find the cost of one pen we must know how many pens he bought.

qa.q: 'A tank fills buckets. How many buckets can it fill?' Which fact is needed?
qa.a: How much the tank and one bucket hold
qa.e: We need the tank's capacity and a bucket's capacity to divide.

qa.q: A sandwich needs 2 slices of bread and 1 cheese slice. You have 20 bread slices and 8 cheese slices. How many sandwiches can you make?
qa.e: Bread allows 20 ÷ 2 = 10, cheese allows 8. The smaller is 8.

qa.q: A garland needs 12 marigolds and 4 roses. There are 120 marigolds and 32 roses. How many garlands?
qa.e: Marigolds allow 120 ÷ 12 = 10, roses allow 32 ÷ 4 = 8. Only 8 garlands.

qa.q: A kite needs 3 sticks and 1 sheet of paper. There are 25 sticks and 10 sheets. How many kites?
qa.e: Sticks allow 25 ÷ 3 = 8 r 1, sheets allow 10. Only 8 kites.

qa.q: A vegetable seller sold 4 kg of brinjal at ₹30 a kg. What amount goes in the sales record?
qa.e: Amount = quantity × rate = 4 × ₹30 = ₹120.

qa.q: Sales: brinjal ₹120, tomato 5 kg at ₹24/kg, beans 3 kg at ₹45/kg. What is the total?
The record shows ₹180 for onions at ₹36 a kg. How many kg were sold?
qa.e: Quantity = amount ÷ rate = 180 ÷ 36 = 5 kg.

qa.q: Which division or multiplication fact is true?
Which number makes '7 × ☐ = 56' true?
Which number makes '☐ ÷ 6 = 12' true?
Is 'the sum of two odd numbers is even' always, sometimes or never true?
qa.e: The two left-over ones of the odd numbers pair up, so the sum is always even: 3 + 5 = 8, 7 + 9 = 16.

qa.q: Is 'half of an even number is even' always, sometimes or never true?
qa.e: Half of 8 is 4 (even) but half of 10 is 5 (odd).

qa.q: Is 'the product of two odd numbers is even' always, sometimes or never true?
qa.e: Odd × odd is always odd: 3 × 5 = 15, 7 × 9 = 63.

qa.q: Which is a counterexample to 'all multiples of 3 are odd'?
qa.e: 6 is a multiple of 3 but it is even, so the claim is false.

qa.q: Riya claims 'doubling any number gives an even number'. Which is true?
qa.a: Always true, because double means 2 groups, which pair up
qa.e: Any number × 2 can be split into pairs, so it is always even.

qa.q: Which of these is a factor of 20?
qa.e: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 with nothing left over.

qa.q: How many factors does 12 have?
qa.e: The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. That is 6 factors.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT a factor of 24?
qa.e: 24 ÷ 5 = 4 with 4 left over, so 5 is not a factor.

qa.q: Which list shows all the factors of 15?
qa.e: 15 = 1 × 15 = 3 × 5. So the factors are 1, 3, 5 and 15.

qa.q: Arjun wants to share 16 coconuts equally among friends with none left. How many friends could he share with?
qa.e: 16 ÷ 8 = 2 exactly. 3, 5 and 6 leave some over.

qa.q: Which number has only two factors, 1 and itself?
qa.e: 11 can only be 1 × 11, so it is a prime number. 9 = 3 × 3, 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7.

qa.q: What is the biggest factor of 30 that is smaller than 30?
qa.e: 30 = 2 × 15, so 15 is a factor. No number between 15 and 30 divides 30 exactly.

qa.q: Which of these is a multiple of 7?
What is the 5th multiple of 8?
Which list shows multiples of 4?
Coconuts are sold in bundles of 6. Which could be the total number of coconuts sold?
qa.e: 42 = 6 × 7. 34, 40 and 50 are not in the 6 times table.

qa.q: 9 is a factor of 54. So 54 is a ___ of 9.
qa.e: 54 = 9 × 6, so 54 is in the 9 times table. It is a multiple of 9.

qa.q: How many multiples of 5 are there from 1 to 50 (including 50)?
qa.e: 5, 10, 15, … 50. That is 50 ÷ 5 = 10 multiples.

qa.q: Meena counts in 3s starting from 3. Which number will she NOT say?
qa.e: 32 is not in the 3 times table: 3 × 10 = 30 and 3 × 11 = 33.

qa.q: What is the smallest multiple of 9 that is bigger than 50?
qa.e: 9 × 5 = 45 is too small. 9 × 6 = 54 is the first one bigger than 50.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
qa.e: A square has 2 lines through the middles of its sides and 2 through its corners: 4 in all.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
qa.e: Only the up-down and across lines through the middle. The corner-to-corner lines do not work.

qa.q: Which capital letter has a line of symmetry?
qa.e: A has an up-down line of symmetry through its middle.

qa.q: Which capital letter has NO line of symmetry?
qa.e: No fold of S makes the halves match. T, M and U each have an up-down line.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle (all sides equal) have?
qa.e: One line from each corner to the middle of the opposite side: 3 lines.

qa.q: Riya folds a paper along a line and the two halves match exactly. What is the fold line called?
qa.e: A line that splits a shape into two matching halves is a line of symmetry.

qa.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
qa.a: Endless, any line through the centre
qa.e: Every line through the centre of a circle cuts it into two matching halves.

qa.q: Which capital letter has exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
qa.e: H has an up-down line and an across line. A has only an up-down line, E only an across line, and F has none.

qa.q: Which letter can be cut out by folding once down the middle (vertical fold) and drawing half?
qa.e: V has a vertical line of symmetry.

qa.q: Which letter has a horizontal line of symmetry only?
qa.e: E matches top and bottom, but not left and right.

qa.q: Which letter has both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry?
qa.e: X matches left-right and top-bottom.

qa.q: To cut out the letter I with two folds, how much of it do you draw?
qa.e: Two folds make 4 layers, so you draw one quarter.

qa.q: Which letter cannot be made by folding and cutting, because it has no line of symmetry?
qa.e: G does not match itself on any fold line.

qa.q: Ravi folds a paper once and cuts half a letter along the fold. He opens a perfect M. Where was the fold?
qa.a: Down the middle of the M
qa.e: M has a vertical line of symmetry, so the fold ran down its middle.

qa.q: How many of these letters have a vertical line of symmetry: A, U, W, S?
qa.e: A, U and W have one. S does not.

qa.q: Which group has only letters with a horizontal line of symmetry?
qa.e: B, C and K each match top and bottom.

qa.q: A dot is 2 squares to the left of an up-down mirror line. Where is its mirror image?
qa.e: The image is the same distance away on the other side: 2 squares to the right.

qa.q: Meena folds a paper in half and cuts half a heart along the fold. What does she get when she opens it?
qa.a: A full heart with a line of symmetry
qa.e: The fold becomes the line of symmetry, so both halves of the heart match.

qa.q: Riya draws half a butterfly on one side of a mirror line. How should she finish it?
qa.a: Draw the mirror image of the half on the other side
qa.e: The other half must be the flipped (mirror) copy, so the wings match.

qa.q: Which word looks exactly the same in a mirror placed beside it?
qa.e: M and O each have an up-down line of symmetry, and MOM reads the same both ways. D and B do not have an up-down line.

qa.q: Half a design touches an up-down mirror line and is 3 squares wide on its left. When it is completed, how wide is the whole design?
qa.e: The other half is also 3 squares wide: 3 + 3 = 6 squares.

qa.q: A rangoli has 8 equal petals around the centre. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
qa.e: Each petal moves to the next petal's place, 8 times in a full turn.

qa.q: Joseph finishes a symmetrical dot design. The left half has 7 dots and no dot is on the line. How many dots are in the whole design?
qa.e: The right half mirrors the left: 7 + 7 = 14 dots.

qa.q: Harpreet makes a kite shape that is symmetrical about an up-down line. The left edge is 30 cm long. How long is the matching right edge?
qa.e: Mirror halves match exactly, so the right edge is also 30 cm.

qa.q: A ceiling fan has 3 equal blades. After what smallest turn does it look the same?
qa.e: It looks the same 3 times in one full turn: 360° ÷ 3 = 120°.

qa.q: A square looks the same after what smallest turn?
qa.e: A square looks the same 4 times in a full turn: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°.

qa.q: Which capital letter looks the same after a half turn?
qa.e: Turn N upside down and it is still N. A, T and V end up upside down.

qa.q: How many times does a square look the same during one full turn?
A rectangle that is not a square looks the same after what smallest turn?
qa.e: After a quarter turn the long sides stand up, so it looks different. After a half turn (180°) it looks the same.

qa.q: A flower rangoli has 6 equal petals around the centre. After what smallest turn does it look the same?
qa.e: It looks the same 6 times in a full turn: 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.

qa.q: A star has 5 equal points. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
qa.e: Each point moves to the next point's place, so it looks the same 5 times.

qa.q: Which of these does NOT look the same after a quarter turn (90°)?
qa.a: Rectangle that is not a square
qa.e: A long rectangle turned 90° stands on its short side, so it looks different.

qa.q: A paper windmill has 4 blades. After which smallest turn does it look the same?
qa.e: Each 1/4 turn moves every blade into the next blade's place.

qa.q: A rectangle that is not a square is turned. At which turn does it first look the same?
qa.e: After a 1/4 turn it stands on its short side. After a 1/2 turn it matches.

qa.q: Which letter looks the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn?
qa.e: N turned upside down is still N, but a 1/4 turn lays it on its side. A and T change after a 1/2 turn; + already matches after a 1/4 turn.

qa.q: Which shape has rotational symmetry but NO line of symmetry?
qa.e: S matches after a 1/2 turn, but no fold line makes its halves match.

qa.q: How many times does a 4-blade windmill look the same in one full turn (counting the full turn)?
qa.e: At 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and the full turn: 4 times.

qa.q: A design matches after a 1/2 turn. Must it also match after a 1/4 turn?
qa.e: A rectangle matches after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn.

qa.q: Which test checks rotational symmetry?
qa.a: Turn it about its centre and see if it looks the same before a full turn
qa.e: Rotational symmetry is about turning, not folding.

qa.q: A firki has 3 blades all bent the same way. Which is true?
qa.a: It looks the same after a 1/3 turn but has no line of symmetry
qa.e: The bent blades spoil every fold line, but turning by 1/3 moves each blade to the next.

qa.q: Which digit has a horizontal line of symmetry but no vertical one?
qa.e: 3's top and bottom halves match, but its left and right do not.

qa.q: Which digit has both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry?
qa.e: 8 matches left-right and top-bottom.

qa.q: Which number looks the same after a 1/2 turn?
qa.e: Turning 69 upside down: 6 becomes 9 and 9 becomes 6, and their order flips, giving 69 again.

qa.q: Does 69 have a line of symmetry?
qa.e: No fold makes 69 match itself, but a 1/2 turn does.

qa.q: Which number (with stick 1s) has a vertical line, a horizontal line and 1/2-turn symmetry?
qa.e: 1001 matches in a mirror, top to bottom, and upside down.

qa.q: Which 3-digit number has 1/2-turn symmetry?
qa.e: 808 turned upside down is still 808. 880 becomes 088.

qa.q: Which 4-digit number looks the same after a 1/2 turn?
qa.e: Turned upside down, 6889 becomes 6889: the 9 at the end becomes a 6 at the front.

qa.q: Which number has a horizontal line of symmetry only (not vertical)?
qa.e: Each 3 matches top-bottom, but 33 does not match left-right in a mirror.

qa.q: A design has one star at the top. Where must another star go so the design matches after a 1/2 turn?
qa.e: A 1/2 turn sends the top to the bottom.

qa.q: A design has a dot at the top. Which dots must be added for it to match after every 1/4 turn?
qa.e: Each 1/4 turn moves the dot to the next side: right, bottom, left.

qa.q: How can you test a design for rotational symmetry?
qa.a: Trace it and turn the tracing about the centre
qa.e: Turning the tracing shows whether the design fits itself before a full turn.

qa.q: In a 3 × 3 grid, how can two colours be used so it looks the same after every 1/4 turn?
qa.a: 4 corners one colour, 4 edge squares the other
qa.e: Corners turn into corners and edges into edges, so this matches.

qa.q: A square rangoli has the same pattern on every side. How many lines of symmetry can it have at most?
qa.e: A square has 4 lines: 2 through opposite corners and 2 through the middles of opposite sides.

qa.q: Which change makes this design match after a 1/2 turn: a triangle on the left only?
qa.a: Add the same triangle on the right, turned upside down
qa.e: A 1/2 turn moves the left triangle to the right and turns it upside down, so that is the partner it needs.

qa.q: A design looks the same after a 1/4 turn. Does it also look the same after a 1/2 turn?
qa.a: Yes, because two 1/4 turns make a 1/2 turn
qa.e: If it matches after one 1/4 turn, it matches after two of them as well.

qa.q: A design has a line of symmetry going down the middle. What does that mean?
qa.a: Folding along it makes the two halves match
qa.e: A line of symmetry is a fold line where the halves match.

qa.q: A square has an equilateral triangle on each of its 4 sides. How many lines of symmetry?
qa.e: The star matches on both diagonal folds and both middle folds: 4 lines.

qa.q: That 4-triangle star is turned. After which smallest turn does it look the same?
qa.e: Each 1/4 turn moves every triangle to the next side.

qa.q: A square has a triangle on its top side only. What symmetry does it have?
qa.a: 1 line of symmetry, no turn symmetry
qa.e: Folding down the middle matches, but any turn moves the triangle away.

qa.q: A square has triangles on the top and bottom. Does it look the same after a 1/2 turn?
qa.e: A 1/2 turn swaps the top and bottom triangles, so it matches.

qa.q: Does that same design (triangles on top and bottom) match after a 1/4 turn?
qa.e: After a 1/4 turn the triangles are on the left and right.

qa.q: Six equilateral triangles meet at a point to form a hexagon. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
qa.e: Every 1/6 turn moves each triangle into the next place: 6 times.

qa.q: A square has triangles on its top and right sides. Which is true?
qa.a: It has 1 line of symmetry (a diagonal) and no turn symmetry
qa.e: The fold along the diagonal between top and right swaps the two triangles. No turn matches.

qa.q: Which design has BOTH reflection and rotational symmetry?
qa.a: Square with triangles on all 4 sides
qa.e: The 4-triangle star has 4 lines and 1/4-turn symmetry.

qa.q: A carved block shows the letter F facing right. Which way does the print face?
qa.e: Stamping flips the carving, so the print is its mirror image.

qa.q: A block is printed 4 times around a centre, turned by a 1/4 turn each time. What symmetry does the design have?
qa.e: Each print is the previous one turned by 1/4, so the whole design matches after a 1/4 turn.

qa.q: A block is printed twice with a 1/2 turn between prints. After which turn does the design match?
qa.e: The two prints swap places after a 1/2 turn.

qa.q: How many times must you print a block, turning 1/4 each time, to complete a 1/4-turn design?
qa.e: Four quarter turns make a full turn, so 4 prints.

qa.q: Which border shape has rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry?
qa.e: Z matches after a 1/2 turn but has no fold line.

qa.q: Which border shape has both reflection and rotational symmetry?
qa.e: X has fold lines and also matches after a 1/2 turn.

qa.q: Which border shape has reflection symmetry only?
qa.e: A heart matches when folded down the middle, but not after a 1/2 turn.

qa.q: Which vegetable, cut across, gives a print with many matching parts around a centre?
qa.e: Bhindi cut across shows ridges all around its centre, like a star.

qa.q: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
What is the perimeter of a square with side 7 cm?
qa.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 7 = 28 cm.

qa.q: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm. What is its perimeter?
qa.e: Add all three sides: 5 + 6 + 7 = 18 cm.

qa.q: Nani's square table cloth has sides of 2 m. How much lace goes all around it?
qa.e: 4 sides of 2 m each: 4 × 2 = 8 m.

qa.q: A garden is 20 m long and 15 m wide. How long is the fence around it?
The perimeter of a square is 36 cm. How long is each side?
qa.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm.

qa.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is 10 cm. What is its breadth?
qa.e: Length + breadth is half the perimeter: 30 ÷ 2 = 15. Breadth = 15 − 10 = 5 cm.

qa.q: Which has the longer perimeter: a square with side 6 cm, or a rectangle 8 cm by 3 cm?
qa.e: Square: 4 × 6 = 24 cm. Rectangle: 2 × (8 + 3) = 22 cm. 24 > 22.

qa.q: A table cloth is 2 m long and 1 m 50 cm wide. How much lace goes all around it?
Nani uses red lace for half of that 7 m border and gold for the other half. How much red lace?
qa.e: 7 m = 700 cm. Half is 350 cm = 3 m 50 cm.

qa.q: A square cushion has sides of 40 cm. How much lace is needed around it?
Which rectangle has a perimeter of 20 cm?
A rectangle has a perimeter of 24 cm and length 9 cm. What is its breadth?
qa.e: Length + breadth = 24 ÷ 2 = 12. 12 − 9 = 3 cm.

qa.q: How many rectangles with whole-number sides have a perimeter of 16 cm? (2 by 6 and 6 by 2 count as one.)
qa.e: Length + breadth = 8: 1 + 7, 2 + 6, 3 + 5, 4 + 4. That is 4 rectangles.

qa.q: Which two rectangles have the same perimeter?
qa.e: Both have length + breadth = 10, so perimeter 20 cm.

qa.q: A dupatta is 2 m 20 cm long and 80 cm wide. How much lace goes around it?
What is the area of a rectangle 5 cm long and 3 cm wide?
qa.e: Area = 5 × 3 = 15 sq cm.

qa.q: What is the area of a square with side 6 cm?
qa.e: Area = 6 × 6 = 36 sq cm.

qa.q: A shape covers 8 full squares and 4 half squares. What is its area?
qa.e: 4 half squares make 2 full squares. 8 + 2 = 10 square units.

qa.q: Nani's quilt has 7 rows of 5 patches. How many patches are there?
qa.e: 7 rows × 5 patches = 35.

qa.q: Which unit should we use for the area of a notebook cover?
qa.e: Area is measured in square units. A notebook is small, so square centimetres fit.

qa.q: A room floor is 4 m by 3 m. Each tile covers 1 sq m. How many tiles cover the floor?
qa.e: Area = 4 × 3 = 12 sq m, so 12 tiles.

qa.q: A rectangle has an area of 24 sq cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its breadth?
qa.e: Length × breadth = area, so breadth = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 cm.

qa.q: Arjun says the area of a square with side 3 cm is 12 sq cm. What went wrong?
qa.a: He found the perimeter, not the area
qa.e: 4 × 3 = 12 is the perimeter. The area is 3 × 3 = 9 sq cm.

qa.q: Which shape leaves gaps when covering a table?
qa.e: Circles touch only at points, so gaps are left between them.

qa.q: A table top is covered by 12 square tiles. How many half-square triangles would cover it?
qa.e: Each square is 2 triangles: 12 × 2 = 24.

qa.q: The same table (12 squares) is covered with rectangles each made of 2 squares. How many rectangles?
qa.e: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 rectangles.

qa.q: A region needs 18 triangles (each half a square). What is its area in squares?
qa.e: 2 triangles make 1 square: 18 ÷ 2 = 9.

qa.q: Which everyday objects would cover a desk fully, with no gaps?
qa.e: Notebooks are rectangles, which fit edge to edge.

qa.q: Why do we say area is measured by counting units?
qa.a: Area tells how many units cover the surface
qa.e: Area is the amount of surface, counted in units like squares.

qa.q: A desk is covered by 10 squares and 4 half-square triangles. What is the area in squares?
qa.e: 4 triangles = 2 squares. 10 + 2 = 12 squares.

qa.q: Raju measured his table as 8 big rectangles. Each big rectangle is 3 squares. What is the area in squares?
qa.e: 8 × 3 = 24 squares.

qa.q: Shape A covers 14 unit squares and shape B covers 12. Which has the bigger area?
qa.e: 14 squares is more than 12 squares.

qa.q: A 3 by 3 square and a 2 by 5 rectangle are on a grid. Which has more area?
qa.e: 3 × 3 = 9 squares and 2 × 5 = 10 squares.

qa.q: A palm tracing covers 30 full squares and 12 half squares. Estimate the area.
qa.e: 12 halves ≈ 6 full squares. 30 + 6 = 36.

qa.q: When estimating the area of a leaf on a grid, which squares do we ignore?
qa.e: Tiny bits of squares are too small to count.

qa.q: A leaf covers 22 full squares and 8 squares about half covered. About how many square units is its area?
qa.e: 8 halves ≈ 4 squares. 22 + 4 = 26.

qa.q: Riya moves a 1 cm cut-out square across her book cover and fits it 24 times without overlap. What is the area?
qa.e: Each fit is 1 sq cm, so 24 sq cm.

qa.q: Shape P has 10 full and 6 half squares. Shape Q has 12 full squares. Which is bigger?
qa.e: P ≈ 10 + 3 = 13 squares, more than 12.

qa.q: Why is counting grid squares only an estimate for a leaf?
qa.a: Its curved edges cut squares into odd parts
qa.e: The parts of squares on the curved edge are not exact halves.

qa.q: A rectangle is 1 cm by 9 cm. What is its perimeter?
A 4 cm × 4 cm square has area 16 sq cm and perimeter 16 cm. A 1 cm × 9 cm rectangle has area 9 sq cm and perimeter 20 cm. What does this show?
qa.a: A bigger area does not always mean a bigger perimeter
qa.e: The square has more area but less perimeter.

qa.q: Is Trisha's claim 'more area means more perimeter' always true?
qa.e: The 1 × 9 rectangle and the 4 × 4 square show it is false.

qa.q: Four 1 cm squares in a row are moved into a 2 × 2 block. What happens to the area?
qa.e: The same 4 squares cover the same surface.

qa.q: What is the perimeter of four 1 cm squares in a row?
qa.e: The row is 4 cm by 1 cm: 2 × (4 + 1) = 10 cm.

qa.q: What is the perimeter of four 1 cm squares in a 2 × 2 block?
Which shape has a bigger area but a SMALLER perimeter than a 2 cm × 8 cm rectangle (area 16, perimeter 20)?
qa.e: 5 × 4 = 20 sq cm (bigger) and 2 × (5 + 4) = 18 cm (smaller).

qa.q: Six squares in a 1 × 6 strip are rearranged into a 2 × 3 block. How does the perimeter change?
A 2 by 6 rectangle and a 3 by 4 rectangle are made of unit squares. What is the same about them?
qa.e: Both cover 12 squares (2 × 6 = 12, 3 × 4 = 12). Perimeters are 16 and 14.

qa.q: What is the perimeter of a 1 by 12 rectangle?
A 4 by 4 square and a 2 by 6 rectangle both have perimeter 16. Which has the bigger area?
qa.e: Square: 4 × 4 = 16 sq units. Rectangle: 2 × 6 = 12 sq units.

qa.q: Nani has 36 square patches. Which quilt shape uses all of them exactly?
qa.e: 6 × 6 = 36. The others give 35, 32 and 33.

qa.q: A rectangle has an area of 20 sq cm and a length of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
qa.e: Breadth = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 cm. Perimeter = 2 × (5 + 4) = 18 cm.

qa.q: A square has a perimeter of 20 cm. What is its area?
qa.e: Side = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm. Area = 5 × 5 = 25 sq cm.

qa.q: A room is 5 m by 4 m. Carpet costs ₹100 for each square metre. How much does the carpet cost?
Kabir doubles both sides of a 3 cm by 2 cm rectangle to make 6 cm by 4 cm. What happens to the area?
qa.e: Old area: 3 × 2 = 6. New area: 6 × 4 = 24. 24 is 4 times 6.

qa.q: A patchwork shape has 6 whole squares and 8 half squares. What is its area?
qa.e: 8 halves = 4 squares. 6 + 4 = 10.

qa.q: A design has 12 half-square triangles and no whole squares. What is its area?
qa.e: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 squares.

qa.q: A patch pattern has 9 whole squares and 6 half squares. What is its area?
qa.e: 6 halves = 3 squares. 9 + 3 = 12.

qa.q: A small quilt is 3 patches by 3 patches. A bigger one is 6 by 6. How many patches does the bigger one need?
qa.e: 6 × 6 = 36. That is 4 times the 9 patches of the small one.

qa.q: When both sides of a quilt are doubled, how many times as many patches are needed?
qa.e: Double length and double breadth: 2 × 2 = 4 times.

qa.q: A small pattern uses 8 patches. A big quilt has 5 copies of the pattern. How many patches?
qa.e: 5 × 8 = 40 patches.

qa.q: Each patch is 10 cm × 10 cm. What is the area of one patch?
A quilt of 4 × 5 patches has 10 cm square patches. What is the quilt's area?
qa.e: 20 patches × 100 sq cm = 2,000 sq cm.

qa.q: A notebook is 20 cm long and 15 cm wide. What is its area?
What is the perimeter of that 20 cm × 15 cm notebook?
A square Ludo board has side 40 cm. What is its area?
A blackboard is 3 m long and 1 m 20 cm high. What is its perimeter?
An L-shape is made of a 6 × 2 rectangle and a 2 × 3 rectangle. What is its area?
An L-shaped room is a 5 m × 4 m part and a 3 m × 2 m part. What is its area?
A big 8 m × 6 m garden has a 2 m × 2 m pond cut out of a corner. What area is left for grass?
Which tool is best for measuring a classroom floor?
qa.e: A long tape measures metres easily.

qa.q: The short hand is just past 8 and the long hand points to 3. What time is it?
qa.e: Short hand → 8 o'clock. Long hand on 3 → 3 × 5 = 15 minutes.

qa.q: Yoga starts when the clock shows 6:30. The long hand points to which number?
qa.e: 30 minutes is 6 × 5 minutes, so the long hand is on 6.

qa.q: Write 2:30 p.m. in 24-hour time.
qa.e: For p.m. hours, add 12: 2 + 12 = 14.

qa.q: Write 9:15 a.m. in 24-hour time.
qa.e: Morning times keep the same hour: 09:15.

qa.q: A train leaves at 18:20. What is that in 12-hour time?
qa.e: 18 − 12 = 6, and it is after noon: 6:20 p.m.

qa.q: What is 12 midnight in 24-hour time?
qa.e: Midnight starts a new day at 00:00. 12:00 is noon.

qa.q: A flight lands at 23:45. When is that?
qa.e: 23 − 12 = 11, and it is p.m.

qa.q: Which time is the latest in the day?
qa.e: 21:10 is 9:10 p.m., the latest of these.

qa.q: A cricket match starts at 2:00 p.m. and ends at 5:30 p.m. How long does it last?
qa.e: 2:00 to 5:00 is 3 hours. 5:00 to 5:30 is 30 minutes more.

qa.q: A film starts at 6:15 p.m. and lasts 2 hours 20 minutes. When does it end?
School runs from 8:00 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. How long is the school day?
qa.e: 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon is 4 hours. Noon to 1:30 p.m. is 1 hour 30 minutes. Total 5 hours 30 minutes.

qa.q: Meena starts her homework at 4:50 p.m. and finishes at 5:25 p.m. How many minutes does she take?
qa.e: 4:50 to 5:00 is 10 minutes. 5:00 to 5:25 is 25 minutes. 10 + 25 = 35.

qa.q: Kabir's train leaves at 10:45 a.m. The journey takes 50 minutes. When does it arrive?
qa.e: 10:45 + 15 minutes = 11:00. 35 more minutes = 11:35 a.m.

qa.q: Joseph sleeps from 9:30 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. How long does he sleep?
qa.e: 9:30 p.m. to midnight is 2 hours 30 minutes. Midnight to 6:00 a.m. is 6 hours. Total 8 hours 30 minutes.

qa.q: A bus ride takes 1 hour 15 minutes. How many minutes is that?
qa.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 60 + 15 = 75 minutes.

qa.q: Aisha practises the flute for 25 minutes every day for 4 days. How long does she practise in all?
qa.e: 25 × 4 = 100 minutes = 60 + 40 = 1 hour 40 minutes.

qa.q: In a 50 m race, Arjun took 14 seconds, Kabir 12 seconds and Joseph 15 seconds. Who won?
qa.e: The smallest time wins. Kabir took only 12 seconds.

qa.q: In that race, Kabir took 12 seconds and Joseph took 15 seconds. How many seconds faster was Kabir?
qa.e: 15 − 12 = 3 seconds.

qa.q: Which is less time: 1 minute 5 seconds or 58 seconds?
qa.e: 1 minute 5 seconds = 65 seconds. 58 is less than 65.

qa.q: Four relay runners took 15, 14, 16 and 15 seconds. What was the team's total time?
qa.e: 15 + 14 + 16 + 15 = 60 seconds, which is exactly 1 minute.

qa.q: A stopwatch shows 1 minute 20 seconds. How many seconds is that?
qa.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 + 20 = 80 seconds.

qa.q: Meena ran the race in 58 seconds last week and 51 seconds today. By how many seconds did she improve?
qa.e: 58 − 51 = 7 seconds less, so she is 7 seconds faster.

qa.q: Riya ran in 50 seconds, Arjun in 47 seconds and Aisha in 53 seconds. Who came second?
qa.e: Order of times: 47 (Arjun), 50 (Riya), 53 (Aisha). Riya is second.

qa.q: Harpreet's heart beats about 80 times in a minute. About how many times does it beat in 30 seconds?
qa.e: 30 seconds is half a minute. Half of 80 is 40.

qa.q: Which of these takes only a few seconds?
qa.e: A blink is over in less than a second.

qa.q: Sunil skips 12 times in 10 seconds. About how many skips in 1 minute?
qa.e: 60 seconds is 6 lots of 10 seconds: 6 × 12 = 72.

qa.q: Neha writes her name 4 times in 20 seconds. About how many times in 1 minute?
Ria guesses she can clap 50 times in a minute. She times it and claps 85 times. What should she do next time?
qa.e: Checking helps improve estimates: her real number was more than her guess.

qa.q: Which tool is best for timing a 100 m race?
qa.e: A stopwatch measures seconds exactly.

qa.q: Arjun runs 100 m in 18 seconds. Kiran takes 21 seconds. How much faster is Arjun?
qa.e: 21 − 18 = 3 seconds.

qa.q: Which is the best unit to time writing one short word?
qa.e: Writing a word takes only a few seconds.

qa.q: Meena hops 15 times in 15 seconds. At the same speed, how many hops in 1 minute?
qa.e: 1 hop each second: 60 hops in 60 seconds.

qa.q: How long does the seconds hand take to make one full turn?
qa.e: One full turn of the seconds hand is 1 minute = 60 seconds.

qa.q: The seconds hand starts at 12 and stops at 4. How many seconds have passed?
qa.e: Each number is 5 seconds: 4 × 5 = 20.

qa.q: Starting at 12, the seconds hand stops at 11. How many seconds?
qa.e: 11 × 5 = 55 seconds.

qa.q: Where should you draw the seconds hand to show 35 seconds?
qa.e: 35 ÷ 5 = 7, so it points at 7.

qa.q: Where does the seconds hand point after 45 seconds, if it started at 12?
The seconds hand starts at 3 and stops at 8. How many seconds passed?
qa.e: From 3 to 8 is 5 numbers: 5 × 5 = 25 seconds.

qa.q: The seconds hand stops 2 small marks after 6. How many seconds is that from 12?
qa.e: At 6 it is 30 seconds; 2 more small marks add 2 seconds: 32.

qa.q: The seconds hand goes round once and then on to 3. How many seconds in all?
qa.e: One full turn = 60 s, then 15 s more: 75 seconds.

qa.q: How many seconds make 1 minute?
qa.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds.

qa.q: How many seconds are there in 3 minutes?
qa.e: 3 × 60 = 180 seconds.

qa.q: Write 2 minutes 15 seconds in seconds.
qa.e: 2 minutes = 120 seconds. 120 + 15 = 135 seconds.

qa.q: 240 seconds is how many minutes?
qa.e: 240 ÷ 60 = 4 minutes.

qa.q: Which of these takes about one second?
qa.e: A single clap is very quick, about one second.

qa.q: How many seconds are there in 1 hour?
qa.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes, and each minute is 60 seconds. 60 × 60 = 3,600.

qa.q: 90 seconds is the same as…
qa.e: 90 = 60 + 30, so 90 seconds = 1 minute 30 seconds.

qa.q: Riya held her breath for 45 seconds. Arjun held his for 1 minute. How many seconds longer was Arjun?
qa.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 − 45 = 15 seconds.

qa.q: How many minutes are in 4 hours?
qa.e: 4 × 60 = 240 minutes.

qa.q: On a double number line, which minute value lines up with 3 hours?
What sits halfway between 1 hour and 2 hours, in minutes?
qa.e: Halfway between 60 and 120 is 90.

qa.q: A bus journey takes 300 minutes. How many hours is that?
How many minutes are in 2 1/2 hours?
qa.e: 2 hours = 120 minutes, half an hour = 30 minutes. 120 + 30 = 150.

qa.q: A film lasts 135 minutes. How long is that in hours and minutes?
qa.e: 120 minutes = 2 hours, and 15 minutes are left.

qa.q: On a double number line for minutes and seconds, which second value lines up with 5 minutes?
qa.e: 5 × 60 = 300 seconds.

qa.q: A cricket match lasts 7 hours. How many minutes is that?
qa.e: 7 × 60 = 420 minutes.

qa.q: A film ends at 9:10 p.m. It lasts 2 hours 25 minutes. When did it start?
Riya must reach school at 8:00 a.m. The bus takes 35 minutes. When must she catch the bus?
A train reaches at 11:20 a.m. after 3 hours 40 minutes. When did it leave?
A puja ended at 12:30 p.m. after 1 hour 45 minutes. When did it begin?
Cooking takes 50 minutes and the food must be ready at 1:15 p.m. When should cooking start?
qa.e: 1:15 − 15 minutes = 1:00. Then 35 more minutes back: 12:25 p.m.

qa.q: A match started at 3:40 p.m. and lasted 1 hour 35 minutes. When did it end?
A night bus arrives at 6:00 a.m. after 8 hours 30 minutes. When did it leave?
qa.e: 6:00 a.m. − 8 hours = 10:00 p.m. (the night before). Then − 30 minutes = 9:30 p.m.

qa.q: How can you check a start time you worked out backwards?
qa.a: Add the duration to it and see if you get the end time
qa.e: Adding the duration to the start should give the end time.

qa.q: A multiplier box turns 3 into 21. What is the multiplier?
The same box (× 7) gets 8. What comes out?
A box turns 4 into 36 and 6 into 54. What does it turn 9 into?
qa.e: The multiplier is 9 (36 ÷ 4). 9 × 9 = 81.

qa.q: A box turns 5 into 60. What number went in if 84 came out?
15 dots are arranged in 3 equal rows. How many dots are in each row?
Which arrays can be made with 15 dots?
qa.e: Only rows of 1, 3, 5 or 15 fit 15 dots exactly.

qa.q: Which number is NOT a factor of 15, using its arrays?
qa.e: 15 cannot be put in 2 equal rows: 1 dot is left over.

qa.q: A box turns 7 into 49 and 2 into 14. What is the multiplier?
Which number is a factor of 18?
qa.e: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 with nothing left over.

qa.q: Which is a multiple of 7?
Which list shows all the factor pairs of 12?
qa.e: Every pair multiplies to 12, and none is missing.

qa.q: How many factor pairs does 20 have?
qa.e: 1 × 20, 2 × 10, 4 × 5: three pairs.

qa.q: Which number is a factor of every number?
qa.e: Any number divided by 1 leaves no remainder.

qa.q: Which is true about the number 9?
qa.a: 9 is both a factor and a multiple of 9
qa.e: 9 ÷ 9 = 1, and 9 × 1 = 9. So it is both.

qa.q: 4 × 6 = 24. Which statement is true?
qa.a: 6 is a factor of 24 and 24 is a multiple of 6
qa.e: The smaller numbers that multiply to 24 are its factors; 24 is their multiple.

qa.q: What is the missing factor? 36 = 4 × ?
How many different arrays (rectangles) can 12 objects make? (2 × 6 and 6 × 2 count as one.)
Using arrays, which list shows all the factors of 18?
Which number can only be arranged in a single row?
qa.e: 13 has only 1 and 13 as factors.

qa.q: Which of these is a prime number?
qa.e: 37 has only the factors 1 and 37. 39 = 3 × 13, 35 = 5 × 7, 33 = 3 × 11.

qa.q: Why is 21 NOT a prime number?
qa.a: It can be arranged as 3 rows of 7
qa.e: 21 = 3 × 7, so it has more than two factors.

qa.q: How many factors does a prime number have?
qa.e: Exactly two: 1 and itself.

qa.q: Is 1 a prime number?
qa.a: No, it has only one factor
qa.e: A prime needs exactly two different factors. 1 has only one.

qa.q: Which number makes the most arrays?
A rabbit jumps 5 steps at a time from 0. Where is it after 4 jumps?
qa.e: 4 jumps × 5 = 20.

qa.q: A frog jumps 3 steps at a time from 0. Which spot will it land on?
qa.e: 15 = 3 × 5, so the frog lands on 15. 10, 14 and 20 are not multiples of 3.

qa.q: A grasshopper jumps 4 steps at a time from 0. How many jumps does it take to reach 28?
qa.e: 28 ÷ 4 = 7 jumps.

qa.q: A kangaroo starts at 2 and jumps 5 each time: 2, 7, 12, 17, … Where does it land next?
A squirrel starts at 30 and jumps back 6 each time. Where is it after 3 jumps?
A frog jumps 7 steps at a time from 0. Will it land on 50?
qa.a: No, 50 is not a multiple of 7
qa.e: 7 × 7 = 49 and 7 × 8 = 56. The frog jumps over 50.

qa.q: A deer leaps 6 steps at a time from 0. Where does it land on its 10th leap?
A frog starts at 1 and jumps 3 each time: 1, 4, 7, 10, 13, … Which of these will it land on?
qa.e: 13 + 3 = 16. 18, 20 and 21 are not in this pattern.

qa.q: A frog jumps 2 and a rabbit jumps 3, both from 0. Where do they first land on the same spot?
qa.e: Frog: 2, 4, 6. Rabbit: 3, 6. They first meet at 6.

qa.q: Which of these is a common multiple of 4 and 6?
qa.e: 12 is in both lists: 4 × 3 = 12 and 6 × 2 = 12. 16 is only a multiple of 4; 18 only of 6.

qa.q: What is the smallest common multiple of 5 and 10?
qa.e: 10 is a multiple of 5 (5 × 2) and of 10 (10 × 1).

qa.q: A frog jumps 4 and a rabbit jumps 6, both from 0. On a number line from 0 to 30, on how many spots (not counting 0) do both land?
qa.e: Common multiples of 4 and 6 up to 30 are 12 and 24. That is 2 spots.

qa.q: Which number is a common multiple of 3 and 5?
qa.e: 15 = 3 × 5. It is in both times tables. 20 and 25 are only multiples of 5; 18 only of 3.

qa.q: Which list shows all the common multiples of 2 and 5 that are less than 40?
qa.e: A number that is a multiple of both 2 and 5 ends in 0: 10, 20, 30.

qa.q: A rabbit jumps 3 at a time and a kangaroo jumps 9 at a time, both from 0. Where do they first meet?
qa.e: 9 is a multiple of 3 (3 × 3), so they first meet at 9.

qa.q: Is 20 a common multiple of 4 and 6?
qa.a: No, 20 is not a multiple of 6
qa.e: 20 = 4 × 5, but 6 × 3 = 18 and 6 × 4 = 24, so 20 is not a multiple of 6.

qa.q: Which list shows the first five common multiples of 4 and 6?
qa.e: They are multiples of 12, the smallest common multiple.

qa.q: What pattern do the common multiples of 3 and 4 show?
qa.a: They go up by 12 each time
qa.e: 12, 24, 36 … each is 12 more.

qa.q: A frog jumps 4 and a rabbit jumps 6 from 0. Who lands exactly on 30?
qa.e: 30 = 6 × 5, so the rabbit lands there. 30 ÷ 4 leaves a remainder, so the frog does not.

qa.q: Both animals (jumps of 4 and 6) want to reach 24. How many jumps does the rabbit need?
qa.e: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 jumps.

qa.q: How many jumps does the frog (jumps of 4) need to reach 24?
qa.e: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 jumps.

qa.q: A deer jumps 5 and a hare jumps 3 from 0. Which spot do they both land on?
qa.e: 45 is a multiple of both 5 and 3.

qa.q: Which number is NOT a common multiple of 2 and 5?
qa.e: 25 is not even, so it is not a multiple of 2.

qa.q: How many common multiples of 4 and 6 are there from 1 to 50?
qa.e: 12, 24, 36 and 48: four of them.

qa.q: Two bells ring every 6 minutes and every 8 minutes. They ring together at 9:00 a.m. After how many minutes do they ring together again?
qa.e: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. 24 is also a multiple of 6. So after 24 minutes.

qa.q: Riya visits the library every 4 days and Kabir every 6 days. They were both there today. In how many days will they meet there again?
qa.e: Multiples of 6: 6, 12. 12 is also a multiple of 4. They meet in 12 days.

qa.q: Laddoos come in boxes of 6 and pedas in boxes of 4. Meena wants the same number of each. What is the smallest number she can buy of each?
qa.e: 12 is the smallest number in both the 6 and 4 times tables. 2 boxes of laddoos and 3 boxes of pedas.

qa.q: Two strings of Diwali lights blink every 3 seconds and every 5 seconds. They blink together now. After how many seconds will they blink together again?
qa.e: 3 and 5 have no common multiple smaller than 15. 15 = 3 × 5.

qa.q: A blue bus leaves the depot every 10 minutes and a red bus every 15 minutes. Both leave at 8:00 a.m. When do they next leave together?
qa.e: Multiples of 15: 15, 30. 30 is a multiple of 10. 8:00 + 30 minutes = 8:30 a.m.

qa.q: Arjun waters plant A every 2 days and plant B every 5 days. He waters both today. How many days until he waters both on the same day again?
qa.e: Multiples of 5: 5, 10. 10 is a multiple of 2. So 10 days.

qa.q: What is the smallest common multiple of 4 and 8?
qa.e: 8 is a multiple of 4 (4 × 2), so 8 is the smallest common multiple.

qa.q: Aisha's cricket club meets every 3 days and her dance class every 9 days. Both are on Monday. After how many days are both on the same day again?
qa.e: 9 is a multiple of 3, so after 9 days.

qa.q: Which jump size from 0 lands on both 24 and 36?
qa.e: 6 divides 24 (4 jumps) and 36 (6 jumps).

qa.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 24 and 36?
qa.e: These are in both factor lists. 8 is not a factor of 36.

qa.q: What is the only common factor of 12 and 13?
