qa.e: 13 is prime, and 13 does not divide 12. So only 1 is common.

qa.q: Which is a common factor of 15 and 25?
qa.e: 5 divides both 15 and 25.

qa.q: How many common factors do 16 and 24 have?
What is the biggest common factor of 18 and 27?
qa.e: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. Biggest common: 9.

qa.q: Which pair has only 1 as a common factor?
qa.e: 8 = 2 × 2 × 2 and 9 = 3 × 3 share nothing but 1.

qa.q: 24 laddoos and 36 barfis go into equal boxes, each box with only one kind and the same number in each. What is the most sweets per box?
qa.e: The number per box must divide both 24 and 36. The biggest is 12.

qa.q: What are the common factors of 20 and 21?
qa.e: 20 and 21 are consecutive numbers, so only 1 divides both.

qa.q: What are the common factors of 6 and 18?
qa.e: 6 divides 18, so every factor of 6 divides 18 too.

qa.q: Which number is a common factor of ANY two even numbers?
qa.e: Every even number divides by 2.

qa.q: Which pair of odd numbers has a common factor other than 1?
qa.e: 9 and 15 both divide by 3.

qa.q: Which jump size lands on 12 but NOT on 18?
qa.e: 4 divides 12 but not 18. 2, 3 and 6 divide both.

qa.q: Which jump size lands on 20 but not on 15?
qa.e: 10 divides 20 but not 15.

qa.q: Which jump size lands on 15 but not on 20?
qa.e: 3 divides 15 but not 20.

qa.q: Which is true for every pair of consecutive numbers?
qa.e: Any number dividing both would also divide their difference, 1. So only 1 works.

qa.q: Which number is divisible by 2?
qa.e: It ends in 8, an even digit.

qa.q: Which number is divisible by 5?
qa.e: It ends in 5.

qa.q: Which number is divisible by 10?
qa.e: It ends in 0.

qa.q: Is 3,475 divisible by 10?
qa.a: No, it does not end in 0
qa.e: Only numbers ending in 0 are divisible by 10.

qa.q: Which number is divisible by 2, 5 and 10?
qa.e: 560 ends in 0, so it is divisible by all three.

qa.q: Which number is divisible by 5 but NOT by 2?
qa.e: 85 ends in 5: divisible by 5 but odd.

qa.q: Which number is divisible by 2 but NOT by 5?
qa.e: 124 is even but does not end in 0 or 5.

qa.q: How many of these are divisible by 10: 40, 45, 100, 305, 990?
qa.e: 40, 100 and 990 end in 0.

qa.q: Is 0 a factor of 10?
qa.e: A factor times some number must give 10. 0 times anything is 0.

qa.q: Which statement about 0 and 1 is true?
qa.a: 1 is a factor of every number
qa.e: Any number ÷ 1 leaves no remainder.

qa.q: 'The sum of two consecutive numbers is always odd.' True or false?
qa.e: One of them is odd and one is even, and odd + even = odd: 7 + 8 = 15.

qa.q: Which number shows that 'every multiple of 4 is a multiple of 8' is false?
qa.e: 12 is a multiple of 4 but 12 ÷ 8 leaves 4.

qa.q: 'Every multiple of 6 is a multiple of 3.' True or false?
Which is a counterexample to 'all odd numbers are prime'?
qa.e: 9 is odd but 9 = 3 × 3, so it is not prime.

qa.q: 'The product of two consecutive numbers is always even.' True or false?
qa.e: One of them is even, and any number times an even number is even: 4 × 5 = 20.

qa.q: Which statement is false?
qa.a: Every factor of 24 is a factor of 12
qa.e: 8 is a factor of 24 but not of 12, so that statement is false.

qa.q: You are facing North. Which direction is on your right?
qa.e: Facing North, East is on your right.

qa.q: Kabir faces East and turns left. Which way does he face now?
qa.e: A left turn is anticlockwise. From East, anticlockwise goes to North.

qa.q: In which direction does the sun rise?
qa.e: The sun rises in the East every morning.

qa.q: Arjun walks 3 blocks North, then 2 blocks East, then 3 blocks South. Where is he now compared with his start?
qa.e: The 3 blocks North and 3 blocks South cancel out. He is 2 blocks East of his start.

qa.q: Harpreet faces West and turns right. Which way does she face now?
qa.e: A right turn is clockwise. From West, clockwise goes to North.

qa.q: Which direction is halfway between North and East?
qa.e: Halfway between North and East is North-East.

qa.q: Riya walks 4 blocks East and then 4 blocks West. How many blocks is she from where she started?
qa.e: East and West are opposite. 4 − 4 = 0, so she is back at the start.

qa.q: Joseph faces North and turns until he faces South. How many degrees did he turn?
qa.e: North to South is a half turn, which is 180°.

qa.q: Early in the morning Kabir stands facing the rising Sun. Which direction is on his left?
qa.e: The Sun rises in the East, so he faces East. With East in front, North is on the left, South on the right and West behind.

qa.q: On a map with North at the top, a stork is drawn above the lake. Which direction is it from the lake?
qa.e: Above means north on such a map.

qa.q: Ducks are to the west of the lake. Where should Riya draw them?
qa.a: To the left of the lake
qa.e: West is to the left when North is at the top.

qa.q: A peacock is drawn to the right of the lake. Which direction is it from the lake?
qa.e: Right is east on a map with North at the top.

qa.q: The banyan tree is east of the lake. Which direction is the lake from the tree?
qa.e: If A is east of B, then B is west of A.

qa.q: Clues: the parrot is north of the lake, and the owl is south of the parrot but north of the lake. Where is the owl?
qa.a: Between the parrot and the lake
qa.e: South of the parrot and north of the lake puts it between them.

qa.q: A heron is below the lake on the map. Which direction is it from the lake?
qa.e: Below means south.

qa.q: Kites are to the north-east of the lake. Where on the map?
qa.a: Up and to the right of the lake
qa.e: North is up and east is right.

qa.q: Which is the best landmark to describe where a bird is?
qa.e: A landmark must stay in one place.

qa.q: Meena faces north in her room. The bed is on her right. Which wall is the bed near?
qa.e: Facing north, right is east.

qa.q: Facing north, the cupboard is behind Arjun. Which side of the room is it?
qa.e: Behind is the opposite of in front: south.

qa.q: Why do we draw a North arrow on a room map?
qa.a: So anyone can tell the directions on the map
qa.e: The arrow lets readers know which way is north, so they can work out the other directions.

qa.q: From which view is a room map drawn?
qa.e: Maps show places as seen from above.

qa.q: Sara faces east. The window is on her left. Which wall is the window on?
qa.e: Facing east, left is north.

qa.q: On Kabir's room map, the table is near the west wall. If North is at the top of the map, where is the table drawn?
qa.e: West is on the left of a map with North at the top.

qa.q: In a room, the door is on the south wall and the window on the north wall. Which is true?
qa.a: The window is opposite the door
qa.e: North and south walls face each other.

qa.q: Which list correctly names objects to the east of Riya if the bed is east, the desk is west and the shelf is east?
qa.e: The bed and the shelf are both on the east side.

qa.q: Ravi walks north and turns right. Which way is he walking now?
qa.e: A right turn from north is a quarter turn clockwise: east.

qa.q: The bus goes east and turns left. Which way is it going now?
qa.e: A left turn from east is anticlockwise: north.

qa.q: A map shows the park to the north of Sita's house and the market to the south. Which is north of her house?
qa.e: The park lies on the north side.

qa.q: The zoo is 3 blocks from stop A and 5 blocks from stop B. Which stop is nearer?
qa.e: 3 blocks is less than 5 blocks.

qa.q: Going south on MG Road, the bus turns right into Lake Road. Which way is it going?
qa.e: Right from south is clockwise: west.

qa.q: To get from home to school, you go 2 blocks east then 3 blocks north. To come back the same way, what is the first move?
qa.e: Retrace the last move first, in the opposite direction.

qa.q: The temple is east of the bus stop and the zoo is west of it. Kiran is at the bus stop. Which way should she walk to the zoo?
qa.e: The zoo is to the west of the stop.

qa.q: What does 'trace a route on a map' mean?
qa.a: Follow the path from start to end, marking each road and turn
qa.e: Tracing shows the whole path step by step.

qa.q: On a map, what does the key (legend) tell us?
qa.e: The key explains the symbols, like 🏫 for a school.

qa.q: A map shows a place as it looks from…
qa.e: A map is a bird's-eye view, as if looking down from above.

qa.q: On most maps, which direction is at the top?
qa.e: Most maps put North at the top.

qa.q: On a grid map, the school is in column B, row 4. Which square is it in?
qa.e: Column letter first, then row number: B4.

qa.q: On a grid map, Arjun's house is in A1 and the market is in A4, in the same column. How many squares down is the market from his house?
qa.e: From row 1 to row 4 is 4 − 1 = 3 squares.

qa.q: A map shows a whole city on one page. Compared with the real city, the map is…
qa.e: A map shrinks the real place so it fits on paper.

qa.q: Which is the best landmark to tell a friend the way to your house?
qa.a: A big red temple at the corner
qa.e: A landmark should be big and stay in one place. Clouds, bicycles and dogs move!

qa.q: On a grid map, rows are numbered 1 at the top to 5 at the bottom. The park is in C3. Which square is just above it?
qa.e: Moving up one row in the same column: row 3 → row 2. So C2.

qa.q: Red Line: Anand, Bagh, City Centre, Dairy, Eastgate. Blue Line: Fort, Ganga, City Centre, Hill, Ishan. Which is the interchange?
qa.e: City Centre is on both lines.

qa.q: On that map, how many stops from Anand to Eastgate on the Red Line?
qa.e: Anand → Bagh → City Centre → Dairy → Eastgate: 4 stops.

qa.q: To go from Bagh to Hill, where must you change trains?
qa.e: Bagh is on Red and Hill is on Blue; they meet at City Centre.

qa.q: How many stops from Fort to Dairy?
qa.e: Fort → Ganga → City Centre (2), change, → Dairy (3).

qa.q: Which line would you take from Ganga to Ishan?
qa.e: Ganga and Ishan are both on the Blue Line.

qa.q: A legend on a metro map shows ● for a station and ◎ for an interchange. What does ◎ at City Centre tell you?
qa.e: The legend says ◎ means interchange.

qa.q: Tina can go Anand → City Centre → Hill (3 stops) or ride to Eastgate and take a bus (6 stops' time). Which is better to reach Hill fast?
qa.a: The metro route via City Centre
qa.e: Fewer stops usually means less time.

qa.q: How many different stations are on this whole map (Red and Blue lines)?
qa.e: 5 on Red + 5 on Blue = 10, but City Centre is counted twice: 9.

qa.q: Why does a school map need a key?
qa.a: To show what each symbol means
qa.e: The key explains the symbols used.

qa.q: Which is the best symbol for the school library?
qa.e: A symbol should remind readers of the place and be listed in the key.

qa.q: The treasure is '10 steps north of the big tree'. On a map with North at the top, where is it drawn?
qa.e: North is up.

qa.q: Ria hid a ball west of the office. On the map (North at top), which side of the office is ✖?
qa.e: West is on the left.

qa.q: Which clue is the most helpful for finding hidden treasure?
qa.a: 5 steps east of the water tap
qa.e: It gives a landmark, a direction and a distance.

qa.q: What must every good school map have?
qa.a: A key and a North arrow
qa.e: The key explains symbols and the arrow gives direction.

qa.q: Your friend follows your map but cannot find the treasure. What is the best thing to do?
qa.a: Check the positions and clues on the map
qa.e: Checking helps find the mistake in the map or clues.

qa.q: The office is east of the library and the playground is east of the office. Which is farthest east?
qa.e: Library → office → playground going east.

qa.q: An ant walks 2 cm north and then 3 cm east. How far does it walk?
Which route reaches the same point as '2 cm north, 3 cm east'?
qa.e: Both end 3 cm east and 2 cm north of the start.

qa.q: Route A: 2 N, 3 E. Route B: 1 S, 3 N, 3 E. Which is shorter?
What is the shortest grid route length to a point 3 cm north and 4 cm east?
qa.e: Shortest routes never go backwards: 3 + 4 = 7 cm.

qa.q: An ant walks 4 cm east, 1 cm north, 2 cm west and 1 cm north. Where is it from the start?
qa.e: East − west = 4 − 2 = 2 cm east. North = 1 + 1 = 2 cm.

qa.q: After going 2 cm north and 3 cm east, how can the ant go straight back home along the grid?
qa.e: Undo each move in the opposite direction.

qa.q: Which route is NOT a shortest route to 1 cm north and 2 cm east?
qa.a: 1 cm west, 1 cm north, 3 cm east
qa.e: It goes west first, so it is 5 cm long instead of 3 cm.

qa.q: An anthill is 3 cm south and 2 cm west of the ant. How long is the shortest grid route?
What does the position (3, 2) mean?
qa.e: The first number is across, the second is up.

qa.q: Zoo grid: Lion (3, 2), Tiger (2, 3). Are they at the same place?
qa.a: No, the order of numbers matters
qa.e: 3 across 2 up is a different spot from 2 across 3 up.

qa.q: Lion (3, 2), Elephant (1, 4), Zebra (4, 1). Which animal is at 4 across, 1 up?
qa.e: (4, 1) is the zebra.

qa.q: A peacock is 5 squares across and 2 squares up. How do you write its position?
qa.e: Across first, then up: (5, 2).

qa.q: To plot (0, 4), where do you put the dot?
qa.a: 4 straight up from the start, no moves across
qa.e: 0 across means stay on the up line; then 4 up.

qa.q: The bear is at (2, 5). The deer is 3 squares to its right on the same row. Where is the deer?
qa.e: Moving right adds to the across number: 2 + 3 = 5. Up stays 5.

qa.q: Which position is closest to the start (0, 0)?
qa.e: (1, 1) is only 2 squares of walking from the start along the lines.

qa.q: Rhino at (4, 3) moves 2 squares up. What is its new position?
qa.e: Moving up adds to the second number: 3 + 2 = 5.

qa.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 10 km. Two villages are 3 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
On Riya's school map, 1 cm = 100 m. The playground is 7 cm from the gate on the map. How far is it really?
A map scale is 1 cm = 2 km. Two towns are 12 km apart. How far apart are they on the map?
qa.e: Each 2 km takes 1 cm. 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

qa.q: On Aisha's map, 1 cm = 50 km. Two cities are 4 cm apart. How far apart are they really?
A plan of a cricket ground uses 1 cm = 5 m. The ground is 9 cm long on the plan. How long is it really?
Map A uses 1 cm = 1 km. Map B uses 1 cm = 2 km. Both show the same city on the same paper. On which map does the city look bigger?
qa.e: On Map A each km takes 1 cm. On Map B each km takes only half a cm. So the city looks bigger on Map A.

qa.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 25 km. A route has three parts of 2 cm, 3 cm and 1 cm on the map. How long is the real route?
qa.e: Total map length: 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 cm. Real: 6 × 25 = 150 km.

qa.q: A map scale is 1 cm = 20 m. A park is 80 m wide. How wide is it on the map?
A tally shows two bundles of five and 3 more lines. What number is that?
40 children were asked how they come to school. 20 walk. What fraction of the children walk?
In the same survey, 20 children walk and 8 cycle. How many more walk than cycle?
Temperatures this week: Mon 30°, Tue 32°, Wed 29°, Thu 33°. Which day was the hottest?
qa.e: 33° is the highest, so Thursday was the hottest.

qa.q: Favourite part of Diwali: Sweets 15, Diyas 12, Rangoli 9, Lights 4. Which statement is TRUE?
qa.e: 15 is the biggest number, so Sweets got the most votes.

qa.q: In that Diwali survey (15, 12, 9 and 4 votes), how many children voted in all?
Books read this month: Riya 5, Arjun 8, Meena 6, Kabir 5. How many children read more than 5 books?
qa.e: Arjun (8) and Meena (6) read more than 5. Riya and Kabir read exactly 5, which is not more than 5.

qa.q: In a quiz, Team A scored 45 and Team B scored 60. By how many points did Team B win?
qa.e: 60 − 45 = 15 points.

qa.q: Key: 🍎 = 10 apples. A shop's row shows 🍎🍎🍎🍎. How many apples does the shop have?
qa.e: 4 symbols × 10 = 40 apples.

qa.q: Key: ⭐ = 4 children. A row shows 3 and a half ⭐. How many children is that?
qa.e: 3 stars = 12 children. Half a star = 2 children. 12 + 2 = 14.

qa.q: Key: 🏏 = 10 runs. Kabir has 🏏🏏🏏🏏🏏🏏 and Joseph has 🏏🏏🏏. How many more runs did Kabir score?
Key: 🙂 = 5 children. How many 🙂 are needed to show 35 children?
qa.e: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 symbols.

qa.q: Why does a pictograph have a key?
qa.a: So we know how many each symbol stands for
qa.e: Without the key we cannot tell if one symbol means 1, 5 or 10 things.

qa.q: Key: 📚 = 20 books. The library row shows 📚📚 and half a 📚. How many books?
A pictograph will show 200, 350 and 500 visitors at a mela. Which key is the best choice?
qa.e: With 50, the rows need 4, 7 and 10 symbols. Easy to draw and read!

qa.q: Key: 🌸 = 6 flowers. Meena picked 24 flowers. How many 🌸 symbols show this?
qa.e: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 symbols.

qa.q: Pictograph (🛵 = 3 vehicles): Scooters 🛵×6, Motorcycles 🛵×8, Mopeds 🛵×4, E-scooters 🛵×2. How many scooters passed?
qa.e: 6 icons × 3 = 18 scooters.

qa.q: In the two-wheeler pictograph (🛵 = 3), which type passed most often?
qa.e: Motorcycles have the most icons, 8, which is 24 vehicles.

qa.q: Using 🛵 = 3, how many motorcycles passed (8 icons)?
What is the total number of two-wheelers (6, 8, 4 and 2 icons; 🛵 = 3)?
qa.e: 20 icons × 3 = 60 vehicles.

qa.q: How many more motorcycles (8 icons) than mopeds (4 icons) passed, with 🛵 = 3?
If the same data is redrawn with 🛵 = 6, how many icons show the 24 motorcycles?
qa.e: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 icons.

qa.q: With 🛵 = 6, how many icons show the 6 e-scooters?
qa.e: 6 ÷ 6 = 1 icon.

qa.q: Why might we choose 🛵 = 6 instead of 🛵 = 3?
qa.a: To draw fewer icons for big numbers
qa.e: A bigger scale needs fewer icons; the data stays the same.

qa.q: Asha watches TV for 1 hour a day and Ravi for 4 hours. How many more hours does Ravi watch?
qa.e: 4 − 1 = 3 hours.

qa.q: How much more does Asha sleep than Ravi (9 h and 8 h)?
qa.e: 9 − 8 = 1 hour.

qa.q: Who plays more, and by how much (Asha 2 h, Ravi 1 h)?
qa.e: 2 − 1 = 1 hour more for Asha.

qa.q: Ravi's times: sleep 8, school 7, play 1, study 2, TV 4, meals 1, other 1 (hours). What is the total in hours?
On which activity do Asha and Ravi spend the same time?
qa.e: Both spend 7 h at school and 2 h studying.

qa.q: Whose routine is more balanced?
qa.a: Asha's — more sleep and play, less TV
qa.e: Asha sleeps more, plays more and watches less TV.

qa.q: Asha spends 1 h 30 min on meals and Ravi spends 1 h. How many more minutes does Asha spend?
qa.e: 90 − 60 = 30 minutes.

qa.q: If Ravi cuts his TV time by 2 hours and adds it to play, how many hours does he play?
qa.e: 1 + 2 = 3 hours of play.

qa.q: Meena's day: sleep 10 h, school 6 h, play 2 h, homework 2 h, meals 2 h and other. How many hours is 'other'?
In Meena's bar graph, which activity has the longest bar?
qa.e: Sleep, 10 hours, is the most.

qa.q: With the scale 1 square = 1 hour, how many squares long is the bar for 6 hours of school?
qa.e: 6 hours ÷ 1 hour per square = 6 squares.

qa.q: With the scale 1 square = 2 hours, how many squares show 10 hours of sleep?
qa.e: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 squares.

qa.q: Children paste paper strips as long as their index fingers: Ali 6 cm, Bina 5 cm 5 mm, Chetan 6 cm 2 mm. Whose strip is longest?
qa.e: 6 cm 2 mm = 62 mm is the longest.

qa.q: In that strip graph, whose finger is shortest?
qa.e: 5 cm 5 mm = 55 mm is the shortest.

qa.q: What must all the bars in a bar graph have the same?
qa.e: Only the lengths change; widths stay equal so the graph is fair.

qa.q: A bar for homework is 3 squares long and each square is 30 minutes. How long is homework?
qa.e: 3 × 30 = 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes.

qa.q: Favourite fruits in Class 5: Mango 12, Banana 8, Apple 5, Grapes 10. Which fruit has the tallest bar?
qa.e: Mango has the biggest number, 12, so its bar is tallest.

qa.q: Using the same fruit graph (Mango 12, Banana 8), how many more children chose Mango than Banana?
In the fruit graph (Mango 12, Banana 8, Apple 5, Grapes 10), how many children voted in all?
On a bar graph, each line stands for 2 children. A bar reaches 7 lines. How many children does it show?
qa.e: 7 × 2 = 14 children.

qa.q: Runs in each over: Over 1 = 6, Over 2 = 10, Over 3 = 4, Over 4 = 12. Which over had the most runs?
qa.e: Over 4 has the tallest bar with 12 runs.

qa.q: Using the runs graph (6, 10, 4 and 12 runs), how many runs were scored in all 4 overs?
Rainy days: June 8, July 15, August 12, September 6. Which month had the fewest rainy days?
qa.e: September has the shortest bar, 6 days.

qa.q: What does a taller bar on a bar graph tell us?
qa.a: There is more of that thing
qa.e: Bar height shows the number. Taller means more.

qa.q: Food wasted in the canteen (kg): Mon 8, Tue 5, Wed 12, Thu 6, Fri 9. On which day was the most food wasted?
qa.e: Wednesday's bar is the tallest, 12 kg.

qa.q: Using the canteen data, on which day was the least food wasted?
qa.e: Tuesday's bar is the shortest, 5 kg.

qa.q: What is the total food wasted in the week (8, 5, 12, 6, 9 kg)?
How much more food was wasted on Wednesday (12 kg) than on Thursday (6 kg)?
If one child eats about 250 g, how many children could the week's 40 kg feed?
Wednesday is always the day khichdi is served, and most waste happens then. What is a sensible prediction?
qa.a: Next Wednesday may also have high waste
qa.e: Patterns in data help us predict, though we cannot be certain.

qa.q: Which is the best way to reduce food waste in the canteen?
qa.a: Take a small serving and ask for more if still hungry
qa.e: Taking only what you can eat means less is thrown away.

qa.q: What is the average (equal share) of food wasted per day over the 5 days (40 kg total)?
qa.e: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 kg a day.

qa.q: A picture of a park shows: 5 children on swings, 3 dogs, 8 birds, 2 benches, 4 trees and 1 ice-cream cart. Which statement is true?
qa.a: There are more birds than dogs
qa.e: 8 birds and 3 dogs: 8 > 3.

qa.q: In the park picture, how many more birds than dogs are there?
